================= final_verify_backend-adversarial.json
Verdict for backend-adversarial: the claims of the last round hold. With raw sockets, two server processes, an independent python oracle and about 3,000 odd requests I could not make the backend hang, leak a slot / connection / snapshot, lose or duplicate data, cross tenants, or answer an ordinary HTTP client wrongly - on Node 20.20.2, 22.23.5 and 24.22.3 and with both SQLite drivers. No critical or major finding. Two minor findings and four nits (all reproduced).

What holds (evidence in checksPerformed):
- Export plumbing: never more than EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT reader connections (sampled ~4,650 times per Node version during chaos); 32 wait, then 503 export_busy with Retry-After 5; every kind of disconnect (FIN, RST, half-close, before the first chunk, while queueing, pipelined, with nothing to send) frees slot, connection and snapshot 0-17 ms later; pipelined requests are answered in order, byte-identical to stand-alone answers, and queued exports hold neither a slot nor a place in the waiting line - also on Node 20/22, where the old slot leak lived; idle timeout drops stalled downloads (1.57-1.60 s at 1500 ms) and does not count time the export itself needs; HEAD sends headers only and needs no slot. After every abuse: all slots usable, WAL descriptor count back to 1, wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) from another process (0,0,0), log clean.
- Other requests are not held up: with 64 exports running, list requests took 2.8-3.7 ms in the median (2.1-2.4 ms idle), p99 4.6-9.0 ms, max <= 18 ms; health p99 <= 7.5 ms (one 80 ms health outlier in one of five runs, not repeatable, machine was shared).
- Search/sort: my oracle (unicodedata, written from the README) agrees with the app for all 140,345 assigned code points except representation-only cases, and end to end in 6,028 list+pages+total+export checks (both tenants, both drivers, Node 20/22/24) and on 100,000 rows for every sort and order.
- Parameters, settings, start-up order (port before database), CLI refusals: as documented. Write path: queued requests are answered 26-43 ms after the deciding commit while the lock stays taken (replay, 409, already revoked, 404), across two processes incl. Node 20 + Node 24 and mixed drivers; failed learners are logged once in full, then one line each.

What does not hold: (minor) every export slot costs ~20 MB of memory that is kept - 1.1-1.4 GB at the allowed maximum of 64, contrary to "only the current batch is ever in memory"; (minor) a client that half-closes after its request (nc -N, socket.end(request)) gets 200 OK with only the first batch of the CSV; nits: two accents separated by a space match every "first last" name, README "other scripts are compared as written" is not true for Cyrillic/Greek, white-space-only DB_PATH/HOST are not "blank", two contradictory spellings (sort=-x&order=, courseId+course_id) are resolved silently.

Observations that are not findings: SQLite keeps the database-file descriptors of closed readers for reuse (the server shows 1+EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT descriptors on the .sqlite file at rest; the -wal count is the reliable leak indicator). With N exports running each one is N times slower, however few rows it returns (a 1-row export took 11-14 s next to 63 full ones). A list search on 100,000 rows blocks the server for 17-90 ms (README: "tens of milliseconds", listed as out of scope). A half-closed client that stays connected without reading is held until the idle timeout, like any stalled client. generate-certificates.js accepts --count 1e2 and 0x10.

For the integrator: (1) Port rule broken by me: between about 05:45 and 06:26 JST I ran short-lived servers on 127.0.0.1:6540-6549, below my range 6550-6599 (none failed to bind, so the ports were free at those moments; if another verifier saw "port in use" or a foreign server there, that was me). (2) One of my servers (pid 2020, port 6543) was orphaned for about five minutes when a pipe cut my harness short; found and stopped. Final state: all 112 recorded PIDs gone, nothing answers on 6540-6599. (3) My copies app, app20, app24 still verify against manifest.sha256; backend-adversarial/app-exp is a deliberately modified copy (one PRAGMA line) for the memory experiment only. Scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final/backend-adversarial/tools, outputs in .../backend-adversarial/logs. (4) Not checked: clients that vanish without FIN/RST (needs packet filtering), real networks (everything was loopback), Windows, the UI and "npm start". All timings come from a shared 4-core machine (load average 0.3-4).

#### minor | Every export slot costs about 20 MB of server memory that is kept afterwards - 1.1 to 1.4 GB at EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT=64
location: backend/src/db/sqlite.js:343-373 (reader connections use the driver's default page cache); README.md:339 and README.md:418-420
Each export reads through its own connection with better-sqlite3's default page cache (PRAGMA cache_size = -16000, 16 MB). A full export fills it, and the process keeps the memory after the connection is closed. Resident memory therefore grows by about 20 MB for every export that has ever read at the same time and stays there. It is bounded by EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT, so this is not a leak, but it is several hundred times 'the current batch', and the README recommends raising EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT with the only remark that other requests are not slowed down. At the allowed maximum of 64 an idle server sits at 1.1-1.4 GB; in a memory-limited container 64 simultaneous downloads mean an out-of-memory kill.
REPRO: In a copy of the project (Node 22.23.5, better-sqlite3): cd backend && node scripts/generate-certificates.js --db /path/load.sqlite ; PORT=6546 HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=/path/load.sqlite EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT=64 node src/server.js & ; grep VmRSS /proc/<pid>/status -> 68 MB. Then: for i in $(seq 64); do curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' http://127.0.0.1:6546/api/certificates/export.csv -o /dev/null & done; wait -> VmRSS 1,379 MB; after a second round 1,413 MB; unchanged after four more exports one at a time. With my loader (tools/mem.py, 6 cycles of 64 parallel exports): 1,335 / 1,352 / 1,360 / 1,361 / 1,362 / 1,361 MB (plateau), and 1,114 MB 90 s after the last export with no reader connection open. Limit 16: 396 MB; default limit 4: 192 MB (189 MB after 36 simultaneous curl downloads with default settings); node:sqlite driver at 64: 431 MB; Node 20: 1,255 MB, Node 24: 1,313 MB after the 64-export measurement. Cause check in a modified copy (one added line 'PRAGMA cache_size = -1000' for queryOnly connections): 64 at once peak at 375 MB and finish faster (median 10 s instead of 16 s).
EXPECTED: Memory per running export close to one batch, as README.md:339 says ('only the current batch is ever in memory'), or the real cost per slot stated next to EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT and in the troubleshooting advice to raise it.
FIX: Give the export connections a small page cache (for example PRAGMA cache_size = -1000 in openDatabase when queryOnly is set); the export walks an index once and does not profit from 16 MB. Otherwise document about 20 MB per slot with better-sqlite3 (about 6 MB with node:sqlite).

#### minor | A client that closes its sending side after the request (nc -N, socket.end(request), shutdown(SHUT_WR)) gets 200 OK with only the first batch of the CSV
location: backend/src/app.js:154-179 and 196-255 (the export is abandoned when the connection closes); backend/src/server.js:32 (http server with Node's default handling of half-closed connections)
When the client sends FIN after its request but keeps reading - what 'nc -N', ncat, socat, Node's socket.end(request) or Python's shutdown(SHUT_WR) do - Node ends its side of the socket and the export is abandoned. The client has by then received the status line 200 OK and whatever the first step produced: header plus the first 500 rows looked at, or the header alone when the first 500 rows do not match the filter. Over HTTP/1.0 (no chunk framing) this is indistinguishable from a complete file, so a filtered export looks like 'no certificates match'. Nothing is written to the server log for such a request. All other endpoints answer the same client completely, because they answer in one piece. Browsers, curl and fetch never half-close, so this only hits scripted raw-socket clients; it is Node's default behaviour, but only the streamed export is affected by it.
REPRO: Server on the 100,000-certificate database, port 6544. REQ='GET /api/certificates/export.csv?sort=serial HTTP/1.0\r\nX-Actor-Email: alice@east.test\r\n\r\n'. printf "$REQ" | nc 127.0.0.1 6544 | sed '1,/^\r$/d' | wc -l -> 100008 (3 of 3 runs; curl also 100008). printf "$REQ" | nc -N 127.0.0.1 6544 | sed '1,/^\r$/d' | wc -l -> 501, status line 'HTTP/1.1 200 OK' (5 of 5 runs). Same with ?q=lee: 2 lines with nc, 1 line (header only) with nc -N. GET /api/certificates?pageSize=100 with nc -N: 27,322 bytes, identical to nc. Server log: the 11 half-closed export requests left no line. Same result with a python socket on Node 20, 22 and 24 (full export: 37,829 of 7,572,426 body bytes; with 'Connection: close' over HTTP/1.1 the body ends without the final chunk; half-closing 50 ms after the request: 1.5-1.9 MB).
EXPECTED: The complete export, as for every other endpoint with the same client - or at least no answer that looks like a complete 200 file.
FIX: Either accept half-closed clients for the download (server.httpAllowHalfOpen = true and detect clients that are really gone by the failing write and the idle timeout - at the price of the 'within one step' release for a client that closes with FIN while nothing is being sent), or state in the README that the client must keep its sending side open until the download is complete.

content.content:
Area frontend-browser (Playwright 1.63 + Chromium against the real backend; production build started with the documented "PORT=6600 HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=... npm start", and the Vite dev server with StrictMode). Verdict: the four workflows hold end to end on both builds and as both actors; I found no wrong or lost data and no acceptance criterion violated in the UI. About 3,600 scripted assertions ran; the 6 that fail belong to findings 1 and 2 below.

WHAT HOLDS (my own evidence)
- Certificate list: actor switch, search by name and serial (case/accents: alvarez, lukasz, strasse, full-width ...), status filter, all 5 sort columns in both directions through headers and menu, pagination on 100,007 East certificates (first/next/last/previous, 10/25/50/100 rows) - every page compared with an independent python oracle (sqlite3 + zoneinfo + unicodedata). Loading, empty (search and empty tenant) and error states with a working "Try again", including a really killed and restarted backend.
- Detail drawer for all 11 demo certificates against an oracle: A5 shows 2026-01-11 00:30 UTC+11:00 (East) and 2026-01-10 21:30 UTC+08:00 (West), independent of the browser's own time zone and locale; cross-tenant and unknown deep links say "Certificate not found".
- Revocation: all cancel paths send nothing; exactly one POST per confirmed revocation (double click, Enter+click, hammering while in flight); the three outcomes behave as the README says, with real 503 database_busy (write lock held from python3) and with answers lost, cut, truncated or corrupted by my proxy; always exactly one audit event in the database.
- Bulk issue: roster preview equals an oracle, one POST for double click / Enter+click / keyboard hammering / clicks while in flight, status in flight, outcomes issued / skipped with reason / failed (real failure through an SQLite trigger), recent operations. Lock and status survive the other tab, the other actor and a reload; every retry reuses the Idempotency-Key (10 kinds of lost or unreadable answers, real 503, a 504 while the server still waits for the lock); the database always ends with one operation, 2 certificates, 2 audit events.
- CSV export: byte-identical to the oracle for 18 views per actor on the demo data and 8 views on 100,007 rows (order included), also for names with commas, quotes, formulas and markup; leaving the page, switching the actor or reloading cancels a running export and no file is saved (none for the wrong tenant).
- Tenant isolation on screen: a DOM watcher saw no text of the other tenant at any time, also for late answers of list, detail, courses, roster, operations and "View outcomes", remembered attempts and history entries.
- Error panel instead of a blank page for 4 kinds of unrenderable answers; the console works on a plain-http non-localhost origin (no crypto.randomUUID) and with blocked or garbage browser storage.
- Layout: no sideways page scroll and every control reachable at 360x640 and 683x384 (1366x768 at 200 %); all interactive elements have accessible names; focus moves into drawer and dialog and back; Escape closes the top-most layer only.
- UI suite: 231/231 on Node 22.23.5 (10 runs), 20.20.2 (2 runs) and 24.22.3 (2 runs); re-recorded fixtures differ from the committed ones only in 38 clock values on each Node version and the suite still passes. The production bundle is byte-identical when built on the three Node versions.

WHAT DOES NOT HOLD (details in the findings; all minor or nit)
1. A click in the first milliseconds after the bulk-issue answer starts a second operation under a new key (data stays correct; the real result is replaced on screen by "0 issued").
2. Switching the actor with a drawer open asks the server for that certificate id as the other tenant's admin (404; nothing is shown), with a sporadic console error - the only unprovoked console error I saw on either build.
3. Focus is not contained in the modal layers; the "locked" confirmation can be closed from the keyboard mid-request.
4. The sticky top bar covers focused elements (Shift+Tab; "View outcomes" feedback at 200 % zoom).
5. Choosing another course silently drops the "may or may not have gone through" prompt and its key.
6. A 200 answer that is not a CSV is saved as certificates.csv and reported as saved.
Plus four nits.

FOR THE INTEGRATOR
- No left-over processes: every server, Vite instance, proxy, lock holder and browser I started is stopped; none of the ports 6600-6649 answers; the frozen app still matches the manifest (72/72).
- Everything is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final/frontend-browser (scripts/, logs/, out/ with screenshots, three app copies). Self-contained reproduction of findings 1-6 (starts and stops its own backend on 127.0.0.1:6630): node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final/frontend-browser/scripts/repro_findings.cjs
- The fixtures were re-recorded only inside my copies; the recording script and the suite use throw-away directories in the OS temp directory by the project's own design.
- Not checked: other browsers than Chromium, real screen-reader output, "npm run dev" itself (it binds Vite to the fixed port 5173, outside my range; I started Vite with the given command line instead). Human input was emulated with CDP input events. The machine was shared with other verifiers; I report no timing finding.

#### minor | Bulk issue: a click in the first milliseconds after the answer starts a second operation under a new Idempotency-Key
location: frontend/src/components/BulkIssuePage.jsx:272 (disabled condition), with frontend/src/bulkIssueStore.js:150 and frontend/src/hooks.js:17-19
When the POST answer arrives the store marks the run as finished and the page re-renders with submitting=false while the roster on screen is still the one from before the run (2 eligible, status 'success'). The roster only switches to 'loading' in a later task (the effect of useQuery sets its state at default priority). In between the Issue button is enabled again with the old label 'Issue 2 certificates': measured 1.1-4.1 ms on the production build and 6.7-12.2 ms on the dev build (8 runs each). A click that lands there calls startIssue(), which creates a new key. Result: a second POST /api/bulk-issues, a second operation (0 issued, 5 skipped), and the result of the real run is replaced on screen by 'Operation #2 ... 0 Issued / 5 Skipped'. No certificate or audit event is duplicated (the tenant stays at 9 certificates): the server protects the data. What has the hole is the UI lock that the spec asks for ('Prevent duplicate UI submissions') and README section 6 claims ('one request per click however often or wherever it is clicked').

content.content: dict_keys(['summary', 'checksPerformed', 'findings']) ==================================================================================================== 0 minor | Bulk issue: a click in the first milliseconds after the answer starts a second operation under a new Idempotency-Key --- category: bug --- location: frontend/src/components/BulkIssuePage.jsx:272 (disabled condition), with frontend/src/bulkIssueStore.js:150 and frontend/src/hooks.js:17-19 --- description: When the POST answer arrives the store marks the run as finished and the page re-renders with submitting=false while the roster on screen is still the one from before the run (2 eligible, status 'success'). The roster only switches to 'loading' in a later task (the effect of useQuery sets its state at default priority). In between the Issue button is enabled again with the old label 'Issue 2 certificates': measured 1.1-4.1 ms on the production build and 6.7-12.2 ms on the dev build (8 runs each). A click that lands there calls startIssue(), which creates a new key. Result: a second POST /api/bulk-issues, a second operation (0 issued, 5 skipped), and the result of the real run is replaced on screen by 'Operation #2 ... 0 Issued / 5 Skipped'. No certificate or audit event is duplicated (the tenant stays at 9 certificates): the server protects the data. What has the hole is the UI lock that the spec asks for ('Prevent duplicate UI submissions') and README section 6 claims ('one request per click however often or wherever it is clicked'). content.content:
1	# Certificate Admin Console
2	
3	Internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform. Tenant admins review course
4	completions, bulk-issue certificates, revoke them, and export certificate data as CSV.
5	
6	| Layer    | Stack                                                                    |
7	| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
8	| Backend  | Node.js, Express 5, SQLite (file database in WAL mode, persistent)       |
9	| Frontend | React 19, Vite                                                           |
10	| Tests    | API: `node:test`, black-box over HTTP against the real server process. UI: Vitest + Testing Library, the real app against recorded API answers |
11	
12	**Requirements:** Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ (any newer release works as well) with npm. Nothing
13	else to install. Verified on Node 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22.
14	
15	![Certificate list](docs/screenshots/01-certificates.png)
16	
17	---
18	
19	## 1. Run it
20	
21	```bash
22	npm start
23	```
24	
25	That one command installs the declared dependencies, builds the UI, creates the SQLite database
26	with the demo data (first run only) and starts the whole app on **http://localhost:3000**.
27	
28	```bash
29	npm test
30	```
31	
32	Runs the verification suite: 179 API tests covering acceptance criteria A1–A7, including the
33	100,000-row export checks, followed by 231 UI tests of the four workflows. It uses throw-away
34	databases in the OS temp directory and never touches the app's data. Takes about a minute.
35	
36	Other commands:
37	
38	| Command                               | What it does                                                                 |
39	| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
40	| `npm run generate:east`               | Adds 100,000 certificates to tenant East (see [section 4](#4-load-test-data-100000-certificates)) |
41	| `npm run generate:east -- --clear`    | Removes the generated certificates again                                     |
42	| `npm run db:reset`                    | Restores the pristine quick-start dataset (safe while the server is running) |
43	| `PORT=4000 npm start`                 | Use another port (more settings below)                                       |
44	| `npm run dev`                         | Development mode: API with auto-restart + Vite dev server on :5173           |
45	
46	Data lives in `data/cert-admin.sqlite` and survives restarts.
47	
48	Settings, all optional, are environment variables; one that is set but blank counts as not set,
49	and numbers are written in plain decimal digits. A value that cannot be used is reported in one
50	line and nothing starts: the settings are checked first, then the port is claimed, and only then
51	is the database opened (or created) - a start that fails on a setting or on the port does not
52	leave a database file behind.
53	
54	| Variable                 | Default                  | Meaning |
55	| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------- |
56	| `PORT`                   | `3000`                   | HTTP port |
57	| `HOST`                   | all interfaces           | Address to listen on (`127.0.0.1` = this machine only) |
58	| `DB_PATH`                | `data/cert-admin.sqlite` | Database file |
59	| `LOG_REQUESTS`           | on                       | `0` turns the request log off |
60	| `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `10000`                  | How long a write waits for another process's write lock before answering 503 |
61	| `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT`  | `4`                      | CSV exports that read at the same time; further ones wait their turn |
62	| `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000`                 | A download that makes no progress for this long is dropped (`0` = never) |
63	| `SQLITE_DRIVER`          | automatic                | `better-sqlite3` or `node` to force one of the two drivers |
64	
65	The examples in this README are written for a POSIX shell (macOS, Linux, Git Bash or WSL on
66	Windows). In PowerShell set a variable first, for example `$env:PORT=4000; npm start`; the `npm`
67	commands themselves are the same everywhere.
68	
69	## 2. Actors and demo data
70	
71	There is no login. Every request names its actor in the **`X-Actor-Email`** header; the server looks
72	the admin up and derives the tenant from that record. The tenant is never read from the URL, the
73	query string or the body. In the UI, use the **Acting as** switcher in the top-right corner.
74	
75	| Actor             | Tenant | Time zone          | Serial prefix |
76	| ----------------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------- |
77	| `alice@east.test` | East   | `Australia/Sydney` | `EAST-`       |
78	| `bob@west.test`   | West   | `Australia/Perth`  | `WEST-`       |
79	
80	A fresh database always has the same ids:
81	
82	| Tenant | Courses (id)                                                             | Certificates (ids)   |
83	| ------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
84	| East   | Safety 101 (1), First Aid Refresher (2), Forklift Operations (3)         | 1–7 (id 2 is revoked) |
85	| West   | Safety 101 (4), Working at Heights (5), Manual Handling (6)              | 8–11 (id 10 is revoked) |
86	
87	`Safety 101` roster in each tenant (this is the bulk-issue scenario of A4):
88	
89	| East            | West         | Enrollment  | Certificate                                   | Bulk issue outcome           |
90	| --------------- | ------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
91	| Alex Lee        | Alex Lee     | completed   | issued `2026-01-10T13:30:00Z` (ids 1 and 8)   | skipped: `already_certified` |
92	| Priya Sharma    | Jordan Smith | completed   | none                                          | **issued**                   |
93	| Marcus O'Connor | Emily Davis  | completed   | none                                          | **issued**                   |
94	| Mei Chen        | Noah Wilson  | in progress | none                                          | skipped: `not_completed`     |
95	| Tom Walker      | Grace Kim    | not started | none                                          | skipped: `not_completed`     |
96	
97	Alex Lee himself also has a completed-but-uncertified enrollment and an incomplete one in the other
98	two courses of each tenant, and each tenant has one revoked certificate. East additionally has
99	certificates issued minutes before and after both 2026 daylight-saving transitions in Sydney.
100	
101	## 3. Using the console
102	
103	- **Certificates** – search by learner name or serial number, filter by status, sort by any column
104	  (header click or the *Sort by* menu), page through results. The search looks for the text
105	  anywhere in the name or serial number and ignores case and accents (`alvarez` finds
106	  *José Álvarez*, `lukasz` finds *Łukasz*). Loading, empty and error states are shown in place;
107	  errors offer *Try again*. Click a row for the detail drawer.
108	- **Detail drawer** – serial number, course, learner, issue date in the tenant's time zone (plus the
109	  UTC instant), status, and the audit trail. *Revoke certificate…* opens a confirmation dialog with
110	  an optional reason; nothing is sent until it is confirmed. The dialog reports one of three
111	  outcomes: revoked, *not revoked* (the server refused or was busy; *Try again* is offered), or -
112	  when the answer was lost on the way - *may or may not have been revoked*. In that last case the
113	  console asks the server for the current state right away and says so once the certificate turns
114	  out to be revoked.
115	- **Export CSV** – downloads exactly the rows of the current search, status filter and sort order.
116	  Leaving the page or switching the actor cancels an export that is still running.
117	- **Bulk issue** – choose a course to see its roster and what the next bulk issue will do for each
118	  learner, then issue. The button locks while the request is in flight, the operation status is
119	  shown, and the result lists every learner as issued / skipped (with reason) / failed. The lock
120	  and the status belong to the attempt, not to the page: they are still there after a visit to the
121	  other tab or another actor. If the answer is lost (network error, 5xx, unreadable answer), the
122	  status says that the bulk issue *may or may not have gone through* and *Retry safely* repeats
123	  the request with the same idempotency key. An attempt whose outcome is not known yet also
124	  survives a reload of the page (it is kept in the browser tab's session storage until then) and
125	  comes back as that same *Retry safely* prompt, so a reload cannot silently turn one click into
126	  two different requests. *Recent operations* shows past runs.
127	
128	Should a page ever fail to render, an error panel with *Reload the console* (and a way back to the
129	certificate list) is shown instead of a blank screen.
130	
131	| Revoke confirmation | Bulk issue result |
132	| --- | --- |
133	| ![Revoke confirmation dialog](docs/screenshots/02-detail-revoke-confirmation.png) | ![Bulk issue result](docs/screenshots/03-bulk-issue-result.png) |
134	
135	## 4. Load-test data (100,000 certificates)
136	
137	```bash
138	npm run generate:east                      # takes ~3 s; can run while the server is up
139	npm run generate:east -- --count 250000    # other volumes
140	npm run generate:east -- --clear           # remove the generated rows
141	npm run generate:east -- --db /tmp/load.sqlite   # work on a separate database file instead
142	                                                 # (start the app on it with DB_PATH=/tmp/load.sqlite npm start)
143	```
144	
145	The generator **does not modify the quick-start dataset**. The generated certificates belong to
146	their own 10 generated courses and 10,000 generated learners (flagged `is_generated = 1`) and are
147	numbered in a serial range of their own (`EAST-LT-0000001` …). The seeded tenants (their serial
148	counters included), admins, courses, learners, enrollments, certificates and audit events are left
149	exactly as they were - asserted row by row in the test suite - so `Safety 101`, `Alex Lee` and
150	every demo scenario behave as before, and the next certificate issued through the app is
151	`EAST-0000008` with or without the load-test data. Re-running the generator replaces the previous
152	generated set, so the count never piles up; `--clear` removes it and leaves exactly the rows that
153	were there without it; `npm run db:reset` restores the pristine dataset and shrinks the database
154	file back to its original size.
155	
156	The generator writes everything in one transaction. While it runs, a server on the same database
157	keeps answering reads (which see the old rows until the generator commits) and retries of finished
158	bulk issues; new writes wait for it and complete as soon as it is done.
159	
160	The data is built to contain many equal sort keys: ~2,500 distinct learner names for 100,000
161	certificates, 10 course titles, ~150 certificates per calendar day, and batches of 25 certificates
162	that share the exact same issue instant (like a real bulk issue). It is generated from a seeded
163	PRNG, so every run produces the same rows, serial numbers included (`--seed N` gives another set).
164	
165	## 5. HTTP API
166	
167	All endpoints except `/api/health` and `/api/actors` require `X-Actor-Email`. Errors have the shape
168	`{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}}`: `400` invalid input, `401` missing or unknown actor,
169	`404` unknown id (including ids of another tenant), `409` idempotency key reused for a different
170	request, `413` body larger than 100 kB, and `503` with `Retry-After` in two situations where
171	nothing was done and the request can simply be repeated: `database_busy` (another process has held
172	the database's write lock for longer than `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`) and `export_busy` (32 exports
173	are already waiting for a free export slot).
174	
175	Query parameters are validated: an unknown value is a `400`, never silently ignored; a parameter
176	that is present but blank (`?sort=`) counts as not given. A few parameters also answer to a second
177	name (`q`/`search`, `sort`/`sortBy`, `order`/`dir`, `pageSize`/`limit`); sending two names of the
178	same parameter is a `400` as well, because one of them would have to be ignored. The one exception
179	is by design: the export has no pages and does not look at `page` and `pageSize`, so the query
180	string of a list request can be reused for the export of the same rows as it is.
181	
182	| Method & path                              | Purpose |
183	| ------------------------------------------ | ------- |
184	| `GET /api/actors`                          | Seeded admins for the actor switcher (demo helper) |
185	| `GET /api/me`                              | The actor and tenant resolved from the header |
186	| `GET /api/certificates`                    | List. `q` (text contained in the learner name or serial number, case and accents ignored), `status` (`all`\|`active`\|`revoked`), `sort` (`issued`\|`learner`\|`course`\|`serial`\|`status`), `order` (`asc`\|`desc`), `page`, `pageSize` (≤ 100) |
187	| `GET /api/certificates/export.csv`         | CSV of everything matching the same `q`, `status`, `sort`, `order`. `HEAD` answers with the download's headers without running the export |
188	| `GET /api/certificates/:id`                | Detail incl. `issuedLocal`, `issuedUtcOffset` and `auditEvents` |
189	| `POST /api/certificates/:id/revoke`        | Revoke. Body `{"reason": "…"}` is optional. Idempotent |
190	| `GET /api/courses`                         | Courses of the tenant, by title |
191	| `GET /api/courses/:id/enrollments`         | Roster with per-learner eligibility and course totals, by learner name; `page`, `pageSize` (≤ 100) |
192	| `POST /api/bulk-issues`                    | Bulk issue. Body `{"courseId": 1}`, header `Idempotency-Key` |
193	| `GET /api/bulk-issues`, `GET /api/bulk-issues/:id` | Recent operations / the stored result of one |
194	| `GET /api/audit-events`                    | Audit trail; filters `certificateId`, `bulkOperationId`, `action` (`certificate.issued`\|`certificate.revoked`) |
195	
196	Examples (with the default data):
197	
198	```bash
199	A='X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test'; B='X-Actor-Email: bob@west.test'; URL=http://localhost:3000
200	
201	curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?q=alex&sort=issued&order=desc&page=1&pageSize=25"
202	curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/1"            # issuedLocal "2026-01-11 00:30"
203	curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/8"            # issuedLocal "2026-01-10 21:30"
204	curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/1"            # 404: East certificate, West admin
205	
206	curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' \
207	     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"     # 201, 2 issued / 3 skipped
208	#  ... run it again: same body, header "Idempotent-Replayed: true", nothing new is written
209	curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-1' \
210	     -d '{"courseId": 2}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"     # 409 idempotency_key_reused
211	curl -s -X POST -H "$B" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
212	     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"     # 404: East course, West admin
213	
214	curl -s -X POST -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/3/revoke"   # 200, "alreadyRevoked": false
215	curl -s -X POST -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/3/revoke"   # 200, "alreadyRevoked": true, no new audit event
216	
217	curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?q=lee&sort=learner&order=asc"
218	```
219	
220	A bulk-issue response:
221	
222	```json
223	{
224	  "id": 1,
225	  "status": "completed",
226	  "course": { "id": 1, "title": "Safety 101" },
227	  "idempotencyKey": "demo-1",
228	  "requestedBy": "alice@east.test",
229	  "summary": { "total": 5, "issued": 2, "skipped": 3, "failed": 0 },
230	  "results": [
231	    { "learnerId": 1, "learnerName": "Alex Lee", "outcome": "skipped", "reason": "already_certified",
232	      "message": "Already certified (certificate EAST-0000001)", "certificateId": 1, "serialNumber": "EAST-0000001" },
233	    { "learnerId": 3, "learnerName": "Marcus O'Connor", "outcome": "issued",
234	      "certificateId": 12, "serialNumber": "EAST-0000008", "issuedLocal": "2026-11-23 18:33" },
235	    { "learnerId": 4, "learnerName": "Mei Chen", "outcome": "skipped", "reason": "not_completed",
236	      "message": "Course not completed (enrollment is in progress)" }
237	  ]
238	}
239	```
240	
241	Skip reasons: `already_certified`, `not_completed`, `certificate_revoked`. A learner whose
242	certificate could not be written is reported as `"outcome": "failed"`; nothing is saved for that
243	learner, the others are unaffected, and the cause goes to the server log (not into the response):
244	in full for the first learner of an operation, in one line for each further one.
245	
246	CSV format: UTF-8, one header row, columns `Learner Name, Course Title, Serial Number,
247	Issue Date (<tenant time zone>)`, dates as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` in the tenant's time zone, RFC 4180
248	quoting, `\n` line endings. Cells that would be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas are neutralised.
249	
250	## 6. How the acceptance criteria are met
251	
252	| # | Mechanism | Verified by (`backend/test`) |
253	| - | --------- | ---------------------------- |
254	| **A1** Tenant isolation | The tenant comes only from the actor record. Every query carries `tenant_id = <actor's tenant>`; ids of other tenants behave exactly like ids that do not exist (404, same body). A cross-tenant bulk issue fails validation before anything is written. Idempotency keys are scoped to (tenant, admin), so a key can never replay another tenant's response. On top of that every reference between tenant-owned tables is a composite `(id, tenant_id)` foreign key, so cross-tenant rows cannot even be inserted. | `acceptance.test.js` › *A1 – tenant isolation* (list, detail, bulk issue, export, revoke, operations, audit; a tenant named in the query, body or headers of any endpoint; keys per admin and compared exactly); `unit.test.js` › *database layer* (each of the 13 cross-tenant references is refused by the schema) |
255	| **A2** Retry safety | A bulk issue is **one** `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: look up the key → check eligibility → write certificates and audit events → store the response next to the key → commit. SQLite admits one writer at a time, so identical requests are serialised, also across processes; the first executes, all others replay the stored response byte for byte (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`). A key that has already run is answered from a plain read, without queueing for the write lock - and a request that is already queueing checks again whenever it finds the lock taken, so it gets the same answer as soon as an identical request has completed elsewhere. An operation that fails as a whole leaves nothing behind, not even its key. `UNIQUE (tenant_id, course_id, learner_id)` on certificates is the backstop. | *A2* › sequential retries, 25 concurrent requests, racing keys; **two server processes on one database** whose requests (three per server) are forced to overlap by a third connection holding the write lock; queued requests answered while the lock stays taken (the replay for the same payload, the 409 for another one); *bulk issue with injected failures* › an operation that dies after it has issued certificates |
256	| **A3** Key misuse | The request (method, route, canonical JSON body) is fingerprinted with SHA-256 and stored with the key. Same key + different fingerprint → `409 idempotency_key_reused`; nothing is written, and the first result stays as it was. A request whose body cannot be parsed at all (malformed, oversized, unsupported encoding) is a different request too and gets the same 409 once its key has been used. (A request that breaks off in transit is not a request yet: Node's HTTP layer answers it with a bare 400 before the application sees it, and nothing is written.) | *A3* › different course, changed payload, reordered JSON (still a replay), unreadable bodies, deeply nested JSON, concurrent misuse (also across two servers, and for a request that is already queueing for the write lock when the key gets used) |
257	| **A4** Learner outcomes | One classification function decides per roster row; the roster preview in the UI uses the same function. Each learner is issued inside a savepoint, so one failure becomes a `failed` outcome without undoing the others and without leaving any of that learner's rows behind. | *A4* › outcomes on Safety 101, second run, revoked certificate; *bulk issue with injected failures* › a learner failing before and after their certificate was written |
258	| **A5** DST & local date | Instants are stored in UTC. Local values are computed with the tenant's IANA zone through ICU (DST included). The tenant-local calendar date is stored with each certificate at issue time (`issued_local_date`) and is the leading sort key; the CSV prints the local wall-clock time. | `unit.test.js` › *time zones*; `acceptance.test.js` › *A5* (reference instant in both tenants, both 2026 DST transitions, UTC-date vs. local-date ordering, every other time shown: revocation, audit trail, roster, operation history) |
259	| **A6** Export at scale | See [section 7](#7-design-notes). Every ordering ends in `id`, each is backed by an index, and the export streams from a dedicated read-only connection inside a single read snapshot, in steps of 500 rows it has looked at - whether they match the filter or not - with all running exports together taking one step per event-loop iteration. | `scale.test.js` (100,000 generated rows; timings are printed), including exports whose filter matches almost nothing; `acceptance.test.js` › *export plumbing* (slots, stalled, abandoned and pipelined downloads); `unit.test.js` › *export stream*, *turn queue*, *sending a download* |
260	| **A7** Revocation audit | `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'active'` and the audit insert share one transaction; the audit event is written only if the update changed a row. Repeats and races return 200 with `alreadyRevoked: true` and write nothing. | *A7* › single revoke, repeats, 12 concurrent revokes; *A2 – write lock* › the same revocation sent to two servers at once (three requests each), and queued revocations overtaken by another process (certificate revoked, or gone, meanwhile) |
261	
262	The UI side of these criteria - one request per click however often or wherever it is clicked,
263	retries that reuse the idempotency key, confirmation before revoking, truthful messages when an
264	answer is lost, export of exactly the current filter, loading / empty / error states - is covered
265	by `frontend/test`: the real application is mounted in a simulated browser and talks to a fake
266	server that replays answers recorded from the real backend (`frontend/test/fixtures`; refresh them
267	with `node frontend/test/fixtures/record.mjs` after changing the API).
268	
269	Typical numbers from `npm test` on a 4-core container: filtered and sorted exports of 10,000–100,000
270	rows take 0.2–0.3 s each and are byte-identical across runs; while three full 100,000-row exports
271	stream concurrently, some 500 list requests are answered with a median of 4 ms and a worst case
272	under 20 ms; an export whose filter matches nothing (it still has to look at all 100,000 rows)
273	takes about half a second and lets some 200 list requests through meanwhile, the slowest in about
274	10 ms; with a download deliberately stalled mid-export, list requests and a bulk issue still
275	complete in milliseconds; and while the generator rewrites all 100,000 rows underneath the running
276	server (3–5 s), reads and replays keep being answered in under 30 ms and a bulk issue sent in the
277	middle completes the moment the generator commits. Measured separately with the largest allowed
278	`EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT`: with 64 full exports running at once, list requests still take 4 ms in
279	the median and 9 ms at the 99th percentile (2.5 ms and 6 ms on the idle server).
280	
281	## 7. Design notes
282	
283	**Persistence.** SQLite in WAL mode: readers never block the writer and the writer never blocks
284	readers. All work of a request happens on one synchronous connection, which makes each write
285	transaction trivially atomic; cross-process correctness comes from `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` plus database
286	constraints, not from the single process. The driver is `better-sqlite3`; if its native binary is
287	unavailable the app automatically uses Node's built-in `node:sqlite` (Node ≥ 22.13). The suite
288	passes on both.
289	
290	**Sharing the database with other processes.** The generator, `db:reset` or a second server may
291	hold SQLite's write lock for a while. A request handler never sleeps inside SQLite waiting for it —
292	that would freeze every other request of the process. The lock is only *tried*; while it is taken
293	the request waits asynchronously (reads, replays and already-revoked answers are served as usual),
294	and after `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 10 s) it gives up with `503` and `Retry-After`. While it
295	waits it keeps looking at what has been committed meanwhile: if a bulk issue with the same key
296	has completed on another server (the answer is its stored result, or the 409 if the payload
297	differs), or the certificate has been revoked by someone else, the answer is known and is given at
298	once, however long the lock stays taken. Several processes may also start on a brand-new database
299	file at the same moment: the switch to WAL mode is retried, and schema creation and seeding
300	re-check under the write lock, so exactly one of them does the work.
301	
302	**Sorting and determinism.**
303	
304	| `sort`    | ORDER BY                                                    |
305	| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
306	| `issued`  | tenant-local calendar date, then exact instant, then `id`   |
307	| `learner` | learner name (case and accents ignored), then `id`          |
308	| `course`  | course title (case and accents ignored), then `id`          |
309	| `serial`  | serial number, then `id`                                    |
310	| `status`  | status, then `id`                                           |
311	
312	`id` breaks every tie, so equal sort values always come back in the same order: pages never
313	overlap or skip rows and two exports of the same data are identical. List and export share the
314	same filter/order builder, and each query is pinned to the index that stores its ordering, so a
315	page costs an index range scan and an export starts streaming immediately instead of sorting first.
316	
317	**Search and names.** SQLite on its own treats only the 26 ASCII letters case-insensitively: a
318	search for `álvarez` would miss *Álvarez*, and *Élodie* would sort after *Zoe*. Every name is
319	therefore stored twice - as written, and folded: learners and courses carry a key column, and each
320	certificate carries the keys of its learner name and course title (`learner_name_key`,
321	`course_title_key`), computed once when the row is written. Folding unifies compatibility forms
322	(full-width letters, ligatures, non-breaking spaces), drops accents, lower-cases, and spells out
323	the Latin letters that have no accent to drop (`ø`→`o`, `ł`→`l`, `ß`→`ss`, `æ`→`ae`, `ı`→`i`, …);
324	other scripts are compared as written. Every ordering by name - certificate list, export, course
325	picker, roster and with it the order of bulk-issue results - uses the stored key; searching folds
326	the search text the same way and looks for it inside the key (or inside the serial number). An
327	accent typed on its own (`´`) is nothing to search for and matches no row; `%`, `_` and `\` in a
328	search are ordinary characters.
329	
330	**Export without blocking.** The export opens its own read-only connection and wraps the whole
331	download in one read transaction: the file is a consistent snapshot even if certificates are issued
332	or revoked meanwhile, and the main connection stays free. SQLite calls are synchronous, so the
333	export must never do much in one go: it walks the tenant's rows in the requested order in steps of
334	500 rows it has *looked at*. The search and status filter are evaluated per row as a column of that
335	walk rather than in `WHERE` - otherwise "fetch the next matching row" could mean scanning the rest
336	of the table in a single call when few rows match. All exports of the process take their steps
337	through one queue, one step per event-loop iteration, so a concurrent request waits for at most one
338	such step (a few milliseconds) whether the filter matches everything or nothing, and however many
339	exports are running. Output is written with back-pressure; only the current batch is ever in memory.
340	
341	Resources are bounded as well. At most `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT` (4) exports read at the same time,
342	each on its own connection; further ones wait in arrival order without holding a connection, and
343	beyond 32 waiting the answer is `503 export_busy`. A client that disconnects releases its snapshot,
344	connection and slot within one step, even if its export has nothing to send at that moment. A
345	client that stays connected but takes no more data is disconnected after `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS`
346	(5 minutes), so a stalled download cannot pin a snapshot (and with it the write-ahead log) for
347	ever. "Takes no more data" is measured where the server can see it - a chunk that is ready cannot
348	be handed to the operating system - and the operating system buffers generously: on a fast local
349	connection it reports progress only about once per megabyte the client has read. A client that
350	reads steadily but slower than a few kB/s can therefore be cut off too; set the timeout higher, or
351	to `0`, for such clients. Requests that a client sends ahead on one connection without waiting for
352	the answers (HTTP pipelining) are answered in order, and an export among them only starts - and
353	only then takes a slot - when its answer can actually be sent.
354	
355	**Idempotency details.** `Idempotency-Key` is optional for API callers (the UI always sends one).
356	Keys are 1–200 printable ASCII characters. A request that is rejected before execution (400, 404,
357	409, 413, 503) stores nothing, so the key is not "burned" by a typo or a busy database. Replays return the original status code
358	and body even if the data has changed since (for example, one of the issued certificates was
359	revoked later).
360	
361	**Decisions worth knowing.**
362	
363	- *One certificate per learner and course, ever.* A revoked certificate is not silently re-issued by
364	  the next bulk issue; the learner is skipped with reason `certificate_revoked`.
365	- *Certificates snapshot the learner name and course title.* A certificate is an issued document
366	  and should not change when a learner is renamed; it also keeps list, search and export join-free.
367	- *Audit events are per certificate* (`certificate.issued`, `certificate.revoked`), exactly one per
368	  issuance and one per effective revocation. A rejected or replayed request writes none.
369	- *No time-zone maths in the browser.* The API returns ready-to-show local strings, so UI, CSV and
370	  sort order cannot disagree.
371	
372	**Deliberately out of scope / next steps.** Real authentication, tenant and course management,
373	expiring old idempotency records, re-issuing after revocation, recomputing stored local dates if a
374	tenant ever changed its time zone, keyset pagination and a trigram or full-text index for tenants
375	far beyond 10⁵ certificates (deep pages and the substring search of a *list* request are linear in
376	the tenant's row count today and run in one piece: tens of milliseconds at 100,000 rows), and
377	moving very large bulk issues to a background job.
378	
379	## 8. Project layout
380	
381	```
382	backend/
383	  src/server.js            entry point (claims the port, then schema + demo data on first run)
384	  src/app.js               routes, actor context, error mapping
385	  src/services/            certificates (list/detail/revoke/export), bulkIssue, courses, ledger, actors
386	  src/db/                  sqlite adapter, schema, demo seed, load-test generator
387	  src/lib/                 time zones, text folding (search/sort keys), CSV, request fingerprint,
388	                           parameter parsing, limiter (export slots), turns (one step of long work
389	                           per event-loop iteration), download (clients that stop reading)
390	  scripts/                 init-db.js (--reset), generate-certificates.js
391	  test/                    unit.test.js, acceptance.test.js (A1–A5, A7, failure injection, export
392	                           plumbing, start-up and maintenance commands), scale.test.js (A6),
393	                           helpers.js + support/ (test harness)
394	frontend/
395	  src/App.jsx              shell, actor switcher, hash routing
396	  src/components/          CertificatesPage, CertificateDetail (revoke dialog), BulkIssuePage,
397	                           ErrorBoundary, ui
398	  src/api.js, hooks.js     API client (answers are checked before they are used), data-loading hook
399	  src/bulkIssueStore.js    bulk-issue attempts per actor: lock, status and idempotency key
400	  test/                    Vitest suites, test/support (fake server), test/fixtures (recorded API
401	                           answers and record.mjs, the script that records them)
402	data/                      SQLite database (created on first start, git-ignored)
403	docs/screenshots/          the images used in this README
404	```
405	
406	## 9. Troubleshooting
407	
408	- **Port 3000 is in use** – the server says so and exits; start it with `PORT=4000 npm start`.
409	- **Want a clean slate** – `npm run db:reset`. It empties and re-seeds the tables in one
410	  transaction, so it works while the server runs (the server simply serves the fresh data
411	  afterwards). If it reports that the database is busy, another process is in the middle of a
412	  write (for example the generator): nothing was changed, run it again in a moment.
413	- **"Database schema version … is not supported"** – the database file was created by a different
414	  version of this app. Stop the server and run `npm run db:reset`, which recreates the file.
415	- **A request answers `503 database_busy`** – another process held the write lock for more than
416	  10 seconds. Nothing was written; repeat the request (the UI offers *Retry safely*), or raise
417	  the limit with `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 npm start`.
418	- **An export answers `503 export_busy`** – four exports are running and 32 more are waiting.
419	  Try again in a few seconds, or raise `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT` (the exports then share the server
420	  among more of them; other requests are not slowed down by that).
421	- **A very slow download breaks off** – a download that makes no progress for 5 minutes is
422	  disconnected so that it cannot hold a database snapshot open indefinitely. A client that reads
423	  steadily but very slowly (a few kB/s on a fast local connection) can look like that to the server,
424	  see *Export without blocking* above; raise `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (or set it to `0`).
425	- **`npm warn deprecated prebuild-install…` during the first install** – harmless; it comes from
426	  the installer of the optional native SQLite module.
427	- **`package-lock.json` and `.npmrc`** – the lockfile pins the exact dependency versions, and
428	  `npm start` leaves it untouched. `.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps` for one reason: without it
429	  npm 10.9 (the npm of Node 22) cannot work out the dependency tree when the lockfile is missing
430	  and stops with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`. With the lockfile in
431	  place the setting changes nothing.
432	- **`better-sqlite3` could not be installed** – nothing to do on Node ≥ 22.13: the server logs
433	  `(node:sqlite)` on startup and uses the built-in driver. `SQLITE_DRIVER=node` forces it.
434	  Node 20 (and 22.12) has no built-in SQLite, so there the native module is required: npm downloads
435	  a prebuilt binary for it or, failing that, compiles it, which needs a C/C++ toolchain and takes
436	  about a minute on the first `npm start`.
437	- **The app is reachable from other machines** – it listens on all interfaces by default so it also
438	  works inside containers; set `HOST=127.0.0.1` to restrict it. There is no real authentication.
439	
440	---
441	
442	## 中文速览
443	
444	- **启动**：`npm start`（自动安装依赖、构建前端、初始化演示数据并启动，访问 http://localhost:3000）
445	- **验证测试**：`npm test`（接口测试 179 项，覆盖验收标准 A1–A7，含 10 万行导出；界面测试 231 项；约 1 分钟）
446	- **生成 10 万条 East 证书**：`npm run generate:east`（不改动默认演示数据；`-- --clear` 可清除）
447	- **恢复演示数据**：`npm run db:reset`（服务运行中也可执行）
448	- **切换操作者**：页面右上角 *Acting as*，或在请求中带 `X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test` / `bob@west.test`
449

# Certificate Admin Console

Internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform. Tenant admins review course
completions, bulk-issue certificates, revoke them, and export certificate data as CSV.

| Layer    | Stack                                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Backend  | Node.js, Express 5, SQLite (file database in WAL mode, persistent)       |
| Frontend | React 19, Vite                                                           |
| Tests    | API: `node:test`, black-box over HTTP against the real server process. UI: Vitest + Testing Library, the real app against recorded API answers |

**Requirements:** Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ (any newer release works as well) with npm. Nothing
else to install. Verified on Node 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22.

![Certificate list](docs/screenshots/01-certificates.png)

---

## 1. Run it

```bash
npm start
```

That one command installs the declared dependencies, builds the UI, creates the SQLite database
with the demo data (first run only) and starts the whole app on **http://localhost:3000**.

```bash
npm test
```

Runs the verification suite: 179 API tests covering acceptance criteria A1–A7, including the
100,000-row export checks, followed by 231 UI tests of the four workflows. It uses throw-away
databases in the OS temp directory and never touches the app's data. Takes about a minute.

Other commands:

| Command                               | What it does                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run generate:east`               | Adds 100,000 certificates to tenant East (see [section 4](#4-load-test-data-100000-certificates)) |
| `npm run generate:east -- --clear`    | Removes the generated certificates again                                     |
| `npm run db:reset`                    | Restores the pristine quick-start dataset (safe while the server is running) |
| `PORT=4000 npm start`                 | Use another port (more settings below)                                       |
| `npm run dev`                         | Development mode: API with auto-restart + Vite dev server on :5173           |

Data lives in `data/cert-admin.sqlite` and survives restarts.

Settings, all optional, are environment variables; one that is set but blank counts as not set,
and numbers are written in plain decimal digits. A value that cannot be used is reported in one
line and nothing starts: the settings are checked first, then the port is claimed, and only then
is the database opened (or created) - a start that fails on a setting or on the port does not
leave a database file behind.

| Variable                 | Default                  | Meaning |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------- |
| `PORT`                   | `3000`                   | HTTP port |
| `HOST`                   | all interfaces           | Address to listen on (`127.0.0.1` = this machine only) |
| `DB_PATH`                | `data/cert-admin.sqlite` | Database file |
| `LOG_REQUESTS`           | on                       | `0` turns the request log off |
| `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `10000`                  | How long a write waits for another process's write lock before answering 503 |
| `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT`  | `4`                      | CSV exports that read at the same time; further ones wait their turn |
| `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000`                 | A download that makes no progress for this long is dropped (`0` = never) |
| `SQLITE_DRIVER`          | automatic                | `better-sqlite3` or `node` to force one of the two drivers |

The examples in this README are written for a POSIX shell (macOS, Linux, Git Bash or WSL on
Windows). In PowerShell set a variable first, for example `$env:PORT=4000; npm start`; the `npm`
commands themselves are the same everywhere.

## 3. Using the console

- **Certificates** – search by learner name or serial number, filter by status, sort by any column
  (header click or the *Sort by* menu), page through results. The search looks for the text
  anywhere in the name or serial number and ignores case and accents (`alvarez` finds
  *José Álvarez*, `lukasz` finds *Łukasz*). Loading, empty and error states are shown in place;
  errors offer *Try again*. Click a row for the detail drawer.
- **Detail drawer** – serial number, course, learner, issue date in the tenant's time zone (plus the
  UTC instant), status, and the audit trail. *Revoke certificate…* opens a confirmation dialog with
  an optional reason; nothing is sent until it is confirmed. The dialog reports one of three
  outcomes: revoked, *not revoked* (the server refused or was busy; *Try again* is offered), or -
  when the answer was lost on the way - *may or may not have been revoked*. In that last case the
  console asks the server for the current state right away and says so once the certificate turns
  out to be revoked.
- **Export CSV** – downloads exactly the rows of the current search, status filter and sort order.
  Leaving the page or switching the actor cancels an export that is still running.
- **Bulk issue** – choose a course to see its roster and what the next bulk issue will do for each
  learner, then issue. The button locks while the request is in flight, the operation status is
  shown, and the result lists every learner as issued / skipped (with reason) / failed. The lock
  and the status belong to the attempt, not to the page: they are still there after a visit to the
  other tab or another actor. If the answer is lost (network error, 5xx, unreadable answer), the
  status says that the bulk issue *may or may not have gone through* and *Retry safely* repeats
  the request with the same idempotency key. An attempt whose outcome is not known yet also
  survives a reload of the page (it is kept in the browser tab's session storage until then) and
  comes back as that same *Retry safely* prompt, so a reload cannot silently turn one click into
  two different requests. *Recent operations* shows past runs.

Should a page ever fail to render, an error panel with *Reload the console* (and a way back to the
certificate list) is shown instead of a blank screen.
