PREV: partly fixed | install-docs (minor): a read-only database file is not detected at start-up 
    Fixed in code. The test catches the regression (fails with assertWritable removed) when it can run: as root from a world-readable copy, or as nobody. As root from the hand-over location it is skipped, and the same mutant (R11) survives the full suite. See finding 1. 

====================================================================================================
--- title: The read-only database start-up test is skipped when the suite runs as root from the hand-over location, and the skip message gives the wrong reason; removing assertWritable then goes unnoticed
--- severity: minor
--- category: test-gap
--- description: backend/test/acceptance.test.js:2418-2421 skips the test whenever unprivilegedSpawnOptions() returns null. That happens not only when there is no unprivileged user, but whenever 'nobody' cannot read src/server.js, i.e. whenever an ancestor directory of the checkout is not world-traversable. Here the hand-over location (/tmp/claude-0 is 0700) is such a case; so is the usual root container layout (/root is 0700). The skip reason printed is 'running as root on a system without an unprivileged user that can run this project', yet 'nobody' exists. The run stays green with 'skipped 1' buried in about 280 lines of output. As a consequence, mutant R11 (db.assertWritable() removed from backend/src/bootstrap.js) survives the whole suite in this location: no other test covers the start-up check.
--- reproduction: In my copy under /tmp/claude-0/.../final2/test-quality/app: npm test -> '﹣ a database file that cannot be written to is refused at start-up, not at the first write ... # running as root on a system without an unprivileged user that can run this project', 'ℹ skipped 1'. runuser -u nobody -- node -e 'require("fs").openSync("<copy>/backend/src/server.js","r")' -> EACCES. Mutant R11 (comment out '    db.assertWritable();' in backend/src/bootstrap.js), run with node --test unit.test.js acceptance.test.js: 175 pass, 0 fail, i.e. survives. In a world-readable copy (/tmp/tq-test-quality-root, chmod a+rX) as root the test runs and passes, and with the same edit it fails ('actual: null' after the 20 s start-up timeout). So the test itself is good; only the skip condition hides it.
--- expected: Either the test runs wherever the suite runs as root (for example by copying the files it needs to a temp directory that 'nobody' can read), or the skip says why it really happened ('nobody' cannot read <path>), and the README tells root users that the checkout must be readable by 'nobody' for this test to run.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: backend/test/acceptance.test.js:2418; backend/test/helpers.js:141-154
--- suggestedFix: Give the two causes of a null result separate messages: no unprivileged user, or <file> not readable by uid <n>. Better, copy src/, node_modules and package.json to a temp directory 'nobody' can read before spawning, so the test never depends on where the checkout lives. Mention the condition in the README sentence about the skip.
====================================================================================================
--- title: Flaky UI test: 'gives the page back when a deep link is left with both dialogs open' fails about 2% of runs under load
--- severity: minor
--- category: test-gap
--- description: frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx:818-819 waits until no dialog is in the DOM, then asserts synchronously that no element is inert. The inert attributes are removed in the Dialog's useEffect cleanup. React can run that cleanup after the DOM removal that the waitFor saw, so on a loaded machine the assertion sometimes runs too early. The page itself recovers: in a probe that kept checking with waitFor, inert was always gone within the timeout. So this is a race in the test, not a product bug. It still makes a red 'npm test' possible without any defect.
--- reproduction: Under 4 busy loops: 100x 'npx vitest run test/detail-revoke.test.jsx -t "Dialogs are modal"' -> runs 58 and 80 failed: 'FAIL ... > gives the page back when a deep link is left with both dialogs open', 'AssertionError: expected <header class="topbar" inert>…(3)</header> to be null' at detail-revoke.test.jsx:819:47. A probe replacing line 819 with an immediate check, then waitFor(...toBeNull()), then a log line, run 100x: 99 'ok', 1 'late', 0 failures of the waitFor.
--- expected: The test passes deterministically: it waits for the state it asserts.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx:819
--- suggestedFix: await waitFor(() => expect(document.querySelector('[inert]')).toBeNull()); also check the other tests in that block that assert on [inert] right after a close.
====================================================================================================
--- title: CSV formula-injection triggers TAB and CR are not tested (mutant survives)
--- severity: minor
--- category: test-gap
--- description: backend/src/lib/csv.js neutralises cells that start with = + - @ TAB or CR (FORMULA_TRIGGER = /^[=+\-@\t\r]/), the OWASP list. The unit test 'neutralises spreadsheet formulas' (unit.test.js:75-80) and the acceptance test 'escapes awkward learner names in the export' cover only '=', '+', '@' and '-'. Dropping \t and \r from the pattern goes unnoticed, so a regression would reopen the TAB-prefixed formula vector with learner names under user control.
--- reproduction: In a throw-away copy: edit backend/src/lib/csv.js 'const FORMULA_TRIGGER = /^[=+\-@\t\r]/;' -> 'const FORMULA_TRIGGER = /^[=+\-@]/;', then cd backend && node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/unit.test.js test/acceptance.test.js -> 175 pass, 0 fail.
--- expected: At least one assertion fails, e.g. csvCell('\t=1+1') should start with an apostrophe.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: backend/test/unit.test.js:75-80 (backend/src/lib/csv.js:4)
--- suggestedFix: Add assert.equal(csvCell('\t=SUM(A1)'), "'\t=SUM(A1)") and a CR case (quoted, because CR needs quoting) to 'neutralises spreadsheet formulas'.
====================================================================================================
--- title: createDirectory's tolerance for a directory that already exists (two processes starting at once) has no test
--- severity: nit
--- category: test-gap
--- description: backend/src/db/sqlite.js createDirectory ignores EEXIST so that two processes creating the same new DB_PATH directory at once do not fail. No test exercises that race: turning the tolerance into an unconditional rethrow survives. It only matters when two servers or scripts first open a database in the same missing directory at the same moment.
--- reproduction: In a throw-away copy: backend/src/db/sqlite.js "      if (err.code !== 'EEXIST') throw err; // somebody else created it in the meantime" -> '      throw err;', then node --test --test-concurrency=1 test/unit.test.js test/acceptance.test.js -> 175 pass, 0 fail.
--- expected: A test that opens the same not-yet-existing nested directory from several processes at once (as the existing 'simultaneous-N.sqlite' WAL test does for files) and expects all of them to succeed.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: backend/src/db/sqlite.js:376-381
--- suggestedFix: Extend the 'simultaneous openers' unit test so that its processes open databases in one fresh nested directory.

然后这个是我对于作业的第六章的回答：1. Column Migration & Rollback
Why it fails: During a rolling deployment, old and new versions run at the same time. If you drop `display_name` too early, old instances crash because the column is missing. If you switch reads/writes to `full_name` before creating it, new instances crash. You also lose data and can't safely roll back once `display_name` is dropped.
Safe sequence:

1. Add `full_name` as nullable in the database.
2. Deploy code that writes to both `display_name` and `full_name`, while still reading from `display_name`.
3. Backfill existing `display_name` values into `full_name` in small batches.
4. Deploy code that reads from `full_name` (falling back to `display_name` if null) while keeping dual-writes on.
5. Once confident and no rollback is needed, stop writing to `display_name`.
6. In a later release, drop `display_name`.

2. Stale Cache After Revocation
Why a 5-second TTL doesn't fix it: It doesn't remove the race condition—it just shrinks the window where bad data is served. Even for 5 seconds, a revoked certificate could still look `ACTIVE` to callers, which is a security bug.
How to fix it:

* Version check (best): Give each certificate a monotonically increasing `version` number. When B revokes it, bump the version in the DB and write a `REVOKED` entry (or tombstone) with that new version to the cache. When A tries to write back to the cache, only let the write succeed if A's version is newer than what's already in the cache.
* Locking alternative: Use a per-certificate lock around cache updates/deletes so A's read-and-populate and B's revoke-and-invalidate can't interleave out of order.

3. Cascading Failure & Recovery
Chain of failure: Normally, 1,000 req/s at 20 ms takes about 20 workers. When B slows to 2 seconds, requests hit the 100 ms timeout and retry up to 3 times—turning 1,000 req/s into up to 4,000 calls against B and holding each request open longer. All 50 workers on A get tied up waiting on `/report`, starving every other endpoint on A.
How to fix `/report`:

* Isolate resources: Cap how many workers `/report` (or calls to B) can use at once so other endpoints still have free workers.
* Add a circuit breaker: If B times out or errors too often, trip the circuit breaker and fail fast without calling B until it recovers.
* Cut back retries: Drop aggressive retries when B is struggling (or use a tight retry budget) so you don't flood a slow service.

What `/report` should return when B is unhealthy: Return a fast degraded response—like a cached report if you have one (ideally marked stale), or a quick `503 Service Unavailable` with a `Retry-After` header (or `202 Accepted` if queued for async processing).  然后他的题目是：Answer all three questions in written-answers.md , in your own words. 
1. A service stores user names in users.display_name. A proposed release introduces
users.full_name, changes all application reads and writes to the new column, and drops
display_name in the same deployment. The service uses rolling deployment, so old and new
application instances run concurrently. The release must also support rollback. Explain why
this release can fail and propose a safe sequence of database and application changes.
2. Certificate details are cached for 60 seconds. Request A misses the cache and reads ACTIVE
from the database. Before A writes to the cache, request B revokes the certificate, commits
the database transaction, and deletes the cache entry. A then writes its stale ACTIVE value
into the cache. A colleague proposes reducing the cache TTL to five seconds. Explain why this
does not fix the problem. Redesign the read and revocation paths so that any read starting
after B returns success cannot receive the stale ACTIVE value.
3. Service A has 50 request workers. Every request to its /report endpoint calls Service B with a
100 ms timeout and up to three retries. Traffic to /report remains at 1,000 requests per
second. B's latency suddenly rises from 20 ms to 2 seconds, and unrelated endpoints on A
soon stop responding. Explain the chain of failure, including the effect of retries. Redesign
/report so unrelated endpoints remain available, and state what /report should return when
B is unhealthy 你看看我回答的怎么样

content.text:
方向都对，三题用的都是标准解法（expand/contract、版本化缓存写入、bulkhead + circuit breaker）。主要欠缺是严谨度：Q3 最好，Q1 差几个细节，Q2 最需要补，因为题目要的是“不可能读到”的保证，而你只给了思路。下面只列要点，措辞你自己来（题目要求 in your own words）。

## Q1 列迁移（大约 80 分）

答对的：新旧版本并存时各自崩溃的原因、删列不可回滚、六步顺序整体正确。

建议补的：

- **失败原因少了一条：数据分叉。** 即使两列都在，滚动期间新实例只写 `full_name`、旧实例只写 `display_name`，互相看不到对方的写入；回滚后新版本写的数据对旧代码不可见。这才是必须双写的理由。另外已有行的 `full_name` 全是空的，新代码会读到空名字。
- **每一步都要写明“为什么可回滚”。** 题目明确要求支持 rollback。例如第 4 步能回滚，是因为双写让 `display_name` 一直是最新的。
- **每一步必须完全铺开再做下一步。** 回填要等所有实例都在双写之后才开始，否则旧实例改过的行会留下过期的 `full_name`，而 fallback 只在 NULL 时才生效。切读之前先验证两列不一致的行数为 0。
- **第 5 步漏了“停止读”。** 你只写了停止写 `display_name`，但第 4 步的 fallback 读还在。如果删列时仍有实例的查询引用该列，会直接报错。应该是：先发布一个完全不引用 `display_name` 的版本并铺开，再单独删列。
- **约束。** 如果 `display_name` 是 NOT NULL，第 5 步停止写入后 insert 会失败，要先放开约束。

## Q2 缓存与撤销（大约 70 分）

答对的：TTL 只是缩小窗口；用 version 加 tombstone 代替 delete 是正确方向。

建议补的：

- **TTL 那段可以更有力。** 脏数据是在 B 删除之后才写入的，之后没人会再删它。而且 TTL 越短，cache miss 越多，这个竞态被触发的机会反而更多。
- **比较并写入必须是原子的。** 要用 Redis Lua 脚本或 memcached 的 `cas` 这类操作。你写的“先看再写”如果不是原子的，本身就是同一个竞态。
- **B 的顺序要写清楚。** B 必须在数据库提交、并且缓存更新成功之后才返回 success。缓存写失败时不能返回成功，要重试或让读绕过缓存。否则缓存里原有的 ACTIVE 条目会被之后的读命中。
- **tombstone 的寿命。** 如果 REVOKED 条目 60 秒后过期，而 A 卡得更久，缓存里就没有东西可比较，A 的旧值照样写得进去。可以利用“撤销不可逆”：REVOKED 条目不设过期。
- **加一段保证性的论证。** 用两三句说明为什么 B 返回后开始的读只可能看到 REVOKED：命中缓存是 REVOKED；未命中则读库，库里已提交；迟到的 A 因版本更低被拒绝。
- **锁方案要加限定。** 分布式锁会过期，A 暂停超过锁的租期后仍会写入旧值，最终还是要靠 version 或 fencing token 兜底。所以它不是独立的替代方案。

## Q3 级联故障（大约 85 分）

答对的：20 个 worker 的基线、重试放大、三项隔离措施、降级返回，都到位。

建议补的：

- **把算术写出来。** B 变慢后每个请求占用 worker 4 × 100 ms = 400 ms，是原来的 20 倍。1000 req/s × 0.4 s 需要 400 个 worker，而只有 50 个。A 的吞吐降到约 125 req/s，其余请求每秒积压 875 个，队列无限增长，所有端点都排在后面。
- **重试对 B 的影响。** 超时的调用在 B 那边并没有取消，B 还在为没人等的请求干活，更难恢复。顺带一提，“4000 次调用”是需求量；受 50 个 worker 限制，实际最多约 500 次/秒。
- **bulkhead 要写“满了立即拒绝”。** 如果超出的 `/report` 请求仍在共享队列里排队，其他端点照样被堵。
- **可选加分项。** 重试加退避和 jitter、整个请求设总时限而不是每次尝试各算、熔断器用 half-open 探测恢复。
- **返回值部分已经不错。** 可以强调两点：熔断打开时不再调用 B，响应要在毫秒级返回；返回缓存报告时要明确标注数据的时间。

优先级：先改 Q2（原子性、B 返回前更新缓存、tombstone 不过期、保证性论证），再改 Q1 第 5 步和回滚说明，Q3 加上那组数字即可。

| **A2** Retry safety | A bulk issue is **one** `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction: look up the key → check eligibility → write certificates and audit events → store the response next to the key → commit. SQLite admit

| **A4** Learner outcomes | One classification function decides per roster row; the roster preview in the UI uses the same function. Each learner is issued inside a savepoint, so one failure becomes a `failed` outcome wi
| **A5** DST & local date | Instants are stored in UTC. Local values are computed with the tenant's IANA zone through ICU (DST included). The tenant-local calendar date is stored with each certificate at issue time (`iss
| **A6** Export at scale | See [section 7](#7-design-notes). Every ordering ends in `id`, each is backed by an index, and the export streams from a dedicated read-only connection inside a single read snapshot, in steps o
| **A7** Revocation audit | `UPDATE … WHERE status = 'active'` and the audit insert share one transaction; the audit event is written only if the update changed a row. Repeats and races return 200 with `alreadyRevoked:

The UI side of these criteria - one request per click however often or wherever it is clicked,
retries that reuse the idempotency key, confirmation before revoking, truthful messages when an
answer is lost, export of exactly the current filter, loading / empty / error states - is covered
by `frontend/test`: the real application is mounted in a simulated browser and talks to a fake
server that replays answers recorded from the real backend (`frontend/test/fixtures`; refresh them
with `node frontend/test/fixtures/record.mjs` after changing the API).

Typical numbers from `npm test` on a 4-core container: filtered and sorted exports of 10,000–100,000
rows take 0.2–0.3 s each and are byte-identical across runs; while three full 100,000-row exports
stream concurrently, some 500 list requests are answered with a median of 4 ms and a worst case
under 20 ms; an export whose filter matches nothing (it still has to look at all 100,000 rows)
takes about half a second and lets some 200 list requests through meanwhile, the slowest in about
10 ms; with a download deliberately stalled mid-export, list requests and a bulk issue still
complete in milliseconds; and while the generator rewrites all 100,000 rows underneath the running
server (3–5 s), reads and replays keep being answered in under 30 ms and a bulk issue sent in the
middle completes the moment the generator commits. Measured separately with the largest allowed
`EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT`: with 64 full exports running at once, list requests still take 4 ms in
the median and 9 ms at the 99th percentile (2.5 ms and 6 ms on the idle server).

cd /home/user/cert-admin-console && python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('README.md')
s = p.read_text()
def rep(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, (old[:70], s.count(old))
    s = s.replace(old, new)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- reproduction steps, inside section 6
rep("""The UI side of these criteria - one request per click however often or wherever it is clicked,""",
"""### Reproducing A1–A7 by hand

`npm test` checks all of this automatically. The steps below show each criterion on the running
app instead: start it as in section 1, then use a second terminal (POSIX shell with `curl`;
`node` prints one JSON answer readably). They begin with the quick-start data and are meant to be
run in this order - A3 and A4 use the answers of A2.

```bash
npm run db:reset
A='X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test'; B='X-Actor-Email: bob@west.test'
URL=http://localhost:3000; J='Content-Type: application/json'
```

**A1 – tenant isolation.**

```bash
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates" | grep -o '"serialNumber":"[A-Z]*' | sort | uniq -c   # 7 x EAST
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates" | grep -o '"serialNumber":"[A-Z]*' | sort | uniq -c   # 4 x WEST
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\\n' -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/1"        # East's certificate as West: 404 ...
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\\n' -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/999999"   # ... word for word the answer for an id that does not exist
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\\n' -X POST -H "$B" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: a1' \\
     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                          # East's course as West: 404 "Course not found"
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?pageSize=1" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # East still has 7 certificates,
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/audit-events"            | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # 8 audit events
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                                          # and no operation: {"items":[]}
```

In the UI: act as Bob and open `http://localhost:3000/#/certificates/1` - *Certificate not found*.

**A2 – one key is one operation, sequentially and concurrently.**

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do            # sequential: executed once, then the stored answer
  curl -s -i -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-seq' -d '{"courseId": 2}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" \\
    | grep -iE '^HTTP|^idempotent-replayed'
done                          # 201 + "Idempotent-Replayed: false", then twice 201 + "true"

seq 20 | xargs -P 20 -I{} curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' \\
     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" -o /tmp/a2-{}.json        # 20 requests at once, one key
sort -u /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l                                                    # 1: all twenty answers are the same
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues" | grep -o '"id":[0-9]*,"status"' | wc -l   # 2 operations, one per key
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?pageSize=1" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'     # 10 certificates: 7 + 1 + 2
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/audit-events?action=certificate.issued" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # 10: one issue event each
```

**A3 – the same key with another payload.**

```bash
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\\n' -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' \\
     -d '{"courseId": 3}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                           # 409 idempotency_key_reused
curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" \\
  | cmp - /tmp/a2-1.json && echo 'first result intact'                    # the original request still gets the first answer
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues" | grep -o '"id":[0-9]*,"status"' | wc -l   # still 2 operations
```

**A4 – the outcome of every learner.**

```bash
node -e 'const o = require("/tmp/a2-1.json"); console.log(o.summary);
  for (const r of o.results) console.log(r.learnerName.padEnd(16), r.outcome, r.reason ?? "", r.serialNumber ?? "")'
# { total: 5, issued: 2, skipped: 3, failed: 0 }
# Alex Lee         skipped already_certified EAST-0000001
# Marcus O'Connor  issued  EAST-0000009
# Mei Chen         skipped not_completed
# Priya Sharma     issued  EAST-0000010
# Tom Walker       skipped not_completed
```

A `failed` outcome needs a write that goes wrong for one learner, which cannot be provoked from
outside; the tests do it by injecting the fault (`acceptance.test.js` › *bulk issue with injected
failures*). The Bulk issue page shows the same outcomes, with the reasons in words.

**A5 – tenant-local dates.**

```bash
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/1" | grep -o '"issuedAt":"[^"]*","issuedLocal":"[^"]*"'   # 2026-01-10T13:30:00.000Z -> 2026-01-11 00:30
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/8" | grep -o '"issuedAt":"[^"]*","issuedLocal":"[^"]*"'   # the same instant -> 2026-01-10 21:30
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc" | head -3   # ordered and printed by the Sydney date
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc" | head -3   # ... and by the Perth date
```

**A6 – 100,000 certificates.**

```bash
npm run generate:east                           # about 3 s; the server keeps running
```

--- title: npm run dev keeps running after the API fails to start; with an invalid PORT Vite later crashes with a stack trace
--- severity: minor
--- category: ux
--- description: scripts/dev.mjs starts the API with `node --watch` and Vite at the same moment, without checking the settings or the port first. When the API cannot start, it prints its one line, but `node --watch` then reports "Failed running 'src/server.js'. Waiting for file changes before restarting..." and stays alive. The API child therefore never exits, dev.mjs never stops Vite, and the user is left with a running dev server on :5173. With PORT=abc, Vite's proxy target becomes `http://localhost:abc`, and the first /api request crashes Vite with `TypeError: Invalid URL` and a 15-line stack trace. With the API port taken, Vite proxies /api to whatever process holds that port. The README says a value that cannot be used is reported in one line and nothing starts.
--- reproduction: In a copy installed under Node 22 (port 5173 checked free first):
1. `PORT=abc HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PATH=<dir>/devbad.sqlite npm run dev`. After 6 s the process tree still holds `node --watch src/server.js` and `vite.js`. The log shows the PORT line, then 'Failed running ... Waiting for file changes', and Vite 'ready'. `curl http://127.0.0.1:5173/api/me` then kills Vite with 'TypeError: Invalid URL ... input: http://localhost:abc' plus a stack trace.
2. With a Python socket holding 127.0.0.1:7219: `PORT=7219 HOST=127.0.0.1 npm run dev`. The log shows 'Port 7219 is already in use...', then 'Failed running ... Waiting for file changes', then Vite ready on 5173. Both children were still running after 6 s.
I stopped both runs by process group; 5173 was free afterwards.
--- expected: `npm run dev` ends with the API's one-line message and exits non-zero, without leaving Vite running, as `npm start` does.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: scripts/dev.mjs:20-31
--- suggestedFix: Before spawning, call loadConfig() and checkDatabaseSettings() from backend/src/config.js and db/sqlite.js in dev.mjs and exit with the message. Optionally also probe the port. Alternatively, start the API once without --watch until it is listening, then switch to watch mode.
====================================================================================================
--- title: Relative --db / DB_PATH typed in a subdirectory resolves against the project root, not where the command was typed
--- severity: nit
--- category: docs
--- description: backend/src/config.js documents resolveUserPath as 'Relative paths mean relative to where the command was typed', using INIT_CWD. The root scripts run a nested `npm run ... --workspace backend`, and that nested npm resets INIT_CWD to the project root. A relative path typed in any subdirectory other than backend/ therefore lands in the project root, outside data/ and outside .gitignore. Typed from the root it works by coincidence.
--- reproduction: In the copy ws: `cd data && npm run db:reset -- --db rel3.sqlite` prints 'Database ready at .../ws/rel3.sqlite', not .../ws/data/rel3.sqlite. `ls ws/*.sqlite` shows rel3.sqlite at the root.
--- expected: The file is created in data/rel3.sqlite, as the code comment states. Otherwise the comment should say 'relative to the project root'.
--- reproduced: True
--- location: backend/src/config.js:10-16, package.json scripts db:reset / generate:east
--- suggestedFix: Pass the original INIT_CWD through the root scripts, or fix the comment, and mention in the README that relative paths are taken from the project root.

--- suggestedFix: Add the two scripts and STATIC_DIR to the README tables, or remove them.

NEW RESULT: completeness
I checked what none of the five verifiers named and found no new data-correctness or acceptance problem. Every gap I checked held. The six earlier findings I re-ran are all real; none was a false alarm.

How I built the list: I listed SPEC sections 1-4 and A1-A7, every README statement round4.diff changed, and every source path it added or changed (backend: app.js export reset, bootstrap/assertWritable, config textSetting/LOG_REQUESTS/reachableHost, sqlite.js createDirectory/cache_size/driver message, download.js abandon/failure, bulkIssue courseId/course_id, certificates sort-direction conflict and needle trim, init-db sqlite_stat drop; frontend: useHashRoute go, topbar height, export ref lock and Content-Type check, row-selection guard, modal Dialog/inert/Tab trap, rosterOutdated, picker lock, announcement, Show outcomes, as-typed, page size 5, vite NODE_ENV, dev.mjs). Almost all round-4 paths are named in at least one report. Most of the remainder is data-correctness paths outside round 4, so I checked those against my own copy with my own scripts: an HTTP/SQLite python harness, a node-vs-zoneinfo oracle, and Playwright in Chromium against the built app on ports 7250-7253.

What I found holds (all new evidence):
- **Idempotency keys:** they are scoped per tenant and actor. Bob reusing Alice's exact key runs his own West operation with no replay and no East data. The same key with an East course gives 404 or 409. Alice's replay is unchanged.
- **Concurrent bulk issues with different keys:**
  - 20 different keys at once on one course: one certificate per learner, 11 issued in total, 11 issue audit events.
  - 8 requests over two servers (better-sqlite3 and node:sqlite) on 4 courses: 6,000 certificates with 6,000 distinct serials. The serial counter advanced exactly 6,000, integrity and foreign-key checks are clean, and there were no failed outcomes.
- **The per-learner `failed` outcome through the API:** I injected a SQLite trigger. The operation row is consistent, the failing learner gets no audit event, and a replay after the cause is gone returns the stored failed result and creates nothing. A new key then issues that learner.
- **CSV formula guard:** names starting with = + - @ TAB and CR come out prefixed with an apostrophe. Quotes, commas and line breaks round-trip through python csv.
- **Time conversion:** time.js matches python zoneinfo on 221,578 instants (every 7.5 minutes, Oct 2025 to May 2027, both zones, DST edges, the A5 instant), with 0 mismatches in local time, offset and date. Every stored issued_local_date in the database also matches the oracle.
- **Export snapshot under writes:**
  - Revocations and a bulk issue sent during a slow 100k export answered in 4-21 ms.
  - The export did not contain the new certificates, and the next export did.
  - wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) returned (0,0,0).
- **Generator under a running server (README claim nobody named):** 5,790 list requests during generation saw only totals 7 or 100,007, never anything in between. A bulk issue sent in the middle got 201 just before the generator exited. The comment "about 150 per calendar day" holds (149.5).
- **Large bulk issue:** 10,000 eligible learners took 0.74 s through the API, with 10,000 certificates and audit events, and the replay came back in 0.02 s. List requests waited up to 759 ms meanwhile, but the README lists very large bulk issues (background job) as out of scope, so I do not report it. In the UI the same size sent 1 POST and the result was announced after 0.9 s. The button then read "No eligible learners", and "Show all" drew 10,000 rows in 1.2 s with no console errors.
- **UI export with the status filter** (not named by anyone): status=revoked sorted by learner is byte-identical to the API export. Searching from page 2 at page size 5 goes back to page 1.
- **Verifier claims I re-ran:** A7 holds (12 concurrent revocations of an active certificate: one alreadyRevoked=false, one audit event).

Clean-up: I stopped servers on 7250 (PID 23476), 7252 (15678) and 7253. For 7253 I first killed the wrong PID: 14911 was the subshell that launched it, so I then killed the node process itself, 14912. No port in 7250-7299 answers. I wrote nothing outside /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final2/critic. My scripts are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/final2/critic/tools.

GAP: holds | Concurrent bulk issues with DIFFERENT keys on the same course, and across two server processes and drivers (duplicate certificates, serial collisions, audit counts) 
     did: 20 concurrent different-key requests on a new 12-learner course (one server). Then 8 concurrent requests on 4 courses x 1,500 learners, split over better-sqlite3 (7252) and node:sqlite (7253). Checked certificates, distinct serials, learner/course pairs, the serial counter, audit events, integrity_c
GAP: holds | Per-learner 'failed' outcome through the API (spec 3.2): operation row consistency, no audit event, what a replay and a new key do 
     did: Added a SQLite trigger that aborts the certificate insert for one learner. Checked the response, bulk_issue_operations counts and audit_events. Dropped the trigger, replayed the same key (stored failed result, no certificate created), then sent a new key (issues that learner).

GAP: holds | README: export is a consistent snapshot while certificates are issued or revoked, and writes are not blocked by an export

--- title: Re-run of install-docs findings: npm run dev's API child never exits on a bad setting; relative --db typed in a subdirectory lands in the project root
--- severity: minor
--- category: robustness
--- description: Confirms two existing findings. (1) dev.mjs starts the API with `node --watch`. On an unusable setting the server prints its one line, and --watch then waits for file changes instead of exiting, so dev.mjs's exit handler never fires. (2) `npm run db:reset -- --db critic-rel.sqlite` run from app/docs created app/critic-rel.sqlite.
--- reproduction: (1) cd critic/app/backend && PORT=abc DB_PATH=.../critic/dev.sqlite timeout 6 node --watch src/server.js -> 'PORT must be an integer ...' then 'Failed running ... (2) cd critic/app/docs && npm run db:reset -- --db critic-rel.sqlite -> 'Database ready at .../critic/app/critic-rel.sqlite'.
--- expected: (1) npm run dev stops with the one-line error. (2) The path resolves where the command was typed, or the docs say it resolves against the project root.
--- reproduced: True
--- suggestedFix: (1) In dev.mjs, check the settings (loadConfig) before spawning, or watch the child's output and stop on the first failure. (2) Document that relative paths are relative to the project root.
--- location: scripts/dev.mjs, backend/src/config.js resolveUserPath

      items: {
        type: 'object',

          title: { type: 'string' },
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['critical', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] },
          category: { type: 'string', description: 'bug | regression | docs | test-gap | robustness | ux | accessibility | tooling' },
          location: { type: 'string', description: 'file:line or URL/command' },
          description: { type: 'string' },
          reproduction: { type: 'string', description: 'Exact commands or steps you ran and what you observed.' },

  required: ['summary', 'checksPerformed', 'findings'],
}

const COMMON = `You are one of three independent verifiers of a small software project just before it is handed over. It went through a full verification round; the author then changed code, tests and documentation once more to answer that round's findings. Your job is to check exactly those last changes: prove that one of them is wrong, incomplete or has broken something next to it - or establish, with evidence you produced yourself, that it holds. Be adversarial but honest: report only what you reproduced; do not pad the report with speculation.

THE PROJECT
"Multi-Tenant Certificate Admin Console": an internal admin console where tenant admins review course completions, bulk-issue certificates, revoke them and export them as CSV. Backend: Node.js (ESM), Express 5, SQLite in WAL mode (driver better-sqlite3, automatic fallback to the built-in node:sqlite). Frontend: React 19 + Vite. No login: every API request names its actor in the header X-Actor-Email (alice@east.test -> tenant East; bob@west.test -> tenant West). "npm start" installs, builds the UI, creates the demo database and serves UI + API on one port. "npm test" runs 191 API tests (node:test) and then 253 UI tests (Vitest, simulated DOM).
- The task specification: ${F}/SPEC.md
- The project as it will be handed over (frozen, READ-ONLY, 72 files): ${F}/app   (manifest: ${F}/manifest.sha256). Treat every statement in its README.md as a claim to check.
- The changes to verify, as a diff against the state that was verified before: ${F}/delta.diff  (12 files: README.md, backend/src/db/sqlite.js, backend/src/lib/csv.js, backend/test/*.js, frontend/src/components/ui.jsx, frontend/test/detail-revoke.test.jsx, frontend/test/setup.js, frontend/vite.config.js, package.json, scripts/dev.mjs). Read it first.
- The findings of the previous round that these changes answer (JSON, one file per verifier): ${S}/wfres/r4_frontend-browser.json, r4_backend-adversarial.json, r4_test-quality.json, r4_install-docs.json, r4_completeness.json, r4_spec-acceptance.json.

GROUND RULES
1. Work only inside your own directory ${F}/<your-area>/ (create it). Make your private copy first:  cp -r ${F}/app ${F}/<your-area>/app && chmod -R u+w ${F}/<your-area>/app , then run "npm ci --no-audit --no-fund" in it. Never write to ${F}/app, to /home/user/cert-admin-console, to ${S}/final, ${S}/final2 or to another verifier's directory. 你看看这些要求：2. Product and Technical Constraints
Build an internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform. Tenant admins review
course completions, issue certificates, revoke them, and export certificate data.
Area Constraint
Backend Go, Python, or Node with a mainstream framework. Use SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL. An
in-memory store is not sufficient.
Frontend Vue 3 or React. Vite is optional.
Startup One documented command must install or use declared dependencies, initialize demo
data, and start the complete app. A second command may run verification.
Actor
context
No login UI is needed. Seed one admin per tenant and identify the actor with a header or
token.
Scope
control
Do not add production authentication, cloud deployment, notifications, or unrelated
features. Correct core behavior comes before visual polish.
3. Required Product Scope
Workflow Required behavior
Certificate
list
Select an actor, search by learner name or serial number, paginate, and sort. Show loading,
empty, and error states.
Bulk issue Choose a course and issue to all eligible learners. Disable duplicate UI submission and show
operation status. Return per-learner outcomes: issued, skipped, or failed.
Certificate
detail
Show serial number, course, learner, tenant-local issue date, and status. Support revocation
with confirmation. Audit both issuance and revocation.
CSV
export
Export learner name, course title, serial number, and tenant-local issue date. Preserve
current search and sort. Handle 100,000-row exports as specified in A6.
4. Acceptance Scenarios
Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario. Automated tests are not
mandatory, but they are often the fastest way to verify these cases. We will run our own checks
against your API and UI.
Required demo data
•
Tenant East using Australia/Sydney and West using Australia/Perth .
•
Admins alice@east.test and bob@west.test , each bound only to their own tenant.
•
Both tenants contain a course titled Safety 101 and a learner named Alex Lee .
Include completed, incomplete, and already certified enrollments.
•
A command or script that can generate 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant without
changing the default quick-start dataset.
ID Given Expected
A1. Tenant isolation Bob attempts to access East data
or invoke East-scoped operations
Only West data is accessible. A crosstenant detail request returns 404 or an
equivalent non-revealing response.
through the list, detail, bulk issue,
and export endpoints.
Cross-tenant bulk issue is rejected and
creates no certificates or audit events.
A2. Retry safety Alice sends the same bulk request
with the same idempotency key
sequentially and concurrently.
One logical operation. Each eligible
learner receives at most one certificate.
Each actual issuance has exactly one
audit event. All callers receive the
outcome of the same logical operation,
without additional certificates or audit
events.
A3. Key misuse Alice reuses the same idempotency
key with a different course or
request payload.
Return 409. Do not execute a second
operation or overwrite the first result.
A4. Learner outcomes A course contains completed,
incomplete, and already certified
learners.
Certificates are issued only to eligible
learners. Incomplete and duplicate cases
are skipped with reasons.
A5. DST and local date An East certificate has UTC
timestamp 2026-01-10T13:30:00Z.
A West certificate has the same
timestamp.
East displays 2026-01-11 00:30. West
displays 2026-01-10 21:30. List sorting
and CSV use the tenant-local calendar
date.
A6. Export growth Generate 100,000 East certificates,
including rows with equal values
for the requested sort field. Apply a
search and sort, then run the
export twice. During the first
export, request the certificate list.
Each export completes within 60
seconds. The CSV contains exactly the
matching East rows in the requested
order. Rows with equal sort keys appear
in the same relative order on repeated
exports. The certificate list request
succeeds while the export is running.
A7. Revocation audit Alice revokes a valid certificate,
then repeats the request.
The first request changes status and
writes one revocation audit event. The
repeat does not create duplicate audit
events.
5. Complete AI Interaction Evidence
Submit every interactive AI session used from planning through final documentation, including
rejected suggestions and unsuccessful runs. Do not substitute a curated prompt list or
screenshots.
Artifact Required content
ai/sessions/ Original native exports where available: JSON, JSONL, Markdown, text, or
HTML. Include user prompts, full assistant responses, tool calls, file edits,
commands, errors, timestamps, and model identifiers when the tool records
them.
ai/session-index.csv One row per session: session_id, tool, model, started_at, ended_at, export_file,
purpose, related_commits. Use a consistent timezone.
ai/decision-log.md Trace at least three material decisions: one AI suggestion you accepted, one you
rejected or corrected, and one scope or design tradeoff. Link each decision to
the relevant session ID, verification evidence, and commit.
Tool action evidence If agent commands or edits are absent from the native conversation export,
include the tool's original activity log or an equivalent chronological export.
Keep AGENTS.md and similar files in git.
Completeness
declaration
List every tool used and any export limitation. For a tool without export,
provide a complete chronological text transcript and explain the limitation.
Disclose non-exportable inline autocomplete rather than silently omitting it.
Confirm that Section 6 was completed without AI.
Remove credentials and private third-party data before submission. Use narrow [REDACTED:
reason] replacements without changing the interaction's substance. Large binary files and
dependency caches are not AI interaction evidence.

/**
 * Text folding for search and sort.
 *
 * SQLite on its own only knows that "a" and "A" are the same letter for the 26 ASCII letters: with
 * LIKE or COLLATE NOCASE a search for "álvarez" would not find "Álvarez", and "Élodie" would sort
 * after "Zoe". Names are therefore folded once, in JavaScript, when a row is written, and the
 * folded form is stored next to the name (the `*_key` columns in the schema). Searching and
 * sorting use that stored key, and the search text goes through the same function, so both sides
 * always agree.
 *
 * The folding ignores case and accents:
 *   - compatibility forms are unified (full-width letters, ligatures, non-breaking spaces),
 *   - accents are dropped ("é" -> "e", "Å" -> "a"), and so is an accent typed on its own ("´", "¨"),
 *   - everything is lower-cased, and the two lower-case forms of the Greek sigma are unified,
 *   - the Latin letters that Unicode does not describe as "a base letter plus an accent" are
 *     replaced by the usual plain spelling ("ø" -> "o", "ł" -> "l", "ß" -> "ss", ...; see below).
 *
 * "Accents" are the combining marks U+0300-036F wherever they occur, so Greek and Cyrillic letters
 * lose theirs as well ("ά" -> "α", "й" -> "и"). The marks of other scripts are not accents and
 * stay (Devanagari vowel signs, kana voicing marks ...): apart from case, those scripts are
 * compared as written.
 */

/**
 * Combining accents (U+0300-036F), together with the space that carries one when an accent stands
 * alone: NFKD turns "´" into a space plus a combining acute. Dropping only the mark would leave
 * that space behind, and a search for "´" would find every name that contains a space.
 */
const ACCENTS = / ?[\u0300-\u036f]+/g;

/** Lower-case Latin letters without a decomposition, and how they are usually written without them. */
const PLAIN_SPELLINGS = new Map([
  ['ß', 'ss'],
  ['æ', 'ae'],
  ['œ', 'oe'],
  ['ø', 'o'],
  ['đ', 'd'],
  ['ð', 'd'],
  ['þ', 'th'],
  ['ł', 'l'],
  ['ħ', 'h'],
  ['ŧ', 't'],
  ['ı', 'i'], // Turkish dotless i ("İ" already folds to "i" through its decomposition)
]);
const LETTERS_WITH_PLAIN_SPELLING = new RegExp(`[${[...PLAIN_SPELLINGS.keys()].join('')}]`, 'g');

export function foldText(text) {
  return String(text)
    .normalize('NFKD')
    .replace(ACCENTS, '')
    .toLowerCase()
    .replaceAll('ς', 'σ')
    .replace(LETTERS_WITH_PLAIN_SPELLING, (letter) => PLAIN_SPELLINGS.get(letter))
    .normalize('NFC');
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Differential vocabulary check: words typical of the withheld entries that survive elsewhere."""
import collections, json, re, sys
sys.path.insert(0, '.')
import export_sessions as ex

config = json.load(open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8'))
staged = sys.argv[1]
lines = [l for l in open(config['session_file'], encoding='utf-8') if l.strip()]
out_lines = [l for l in open(staged, encoding='utf-8') if l.strip()]
lines = lines[:len(out_lines)]
entries = [json.loads(l) for l in lines]
unrelated, _ = ex.classify_main(entries, config)

def leaves(node, acc):
    if isinstance(node, str): acc.append(node)
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for x in node: leaves(x, acc)
    elif isinstance(node, dict):
        for k, v in node.items():
            if k in ('signature', 'data', 'base64', 'uuid', 'parentUuid', 'sessionId', 'requestId', 'id', 'tool_use_id'): continue
            leaves(v, acc)
    return acc

LATIN = re.compile(r'[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]{3,}')
CJK = re.compile(r'[一-鿿]{2,}')
def tokens(text):
    c = collections.Counter(w.lower() for w in LATIN.findall(text))
    for run in CJK.findall(text):
        for n in (2, 3):
            for i in range(len(run) - n + 1): c[run[i:i + n]] += 1
    return c

un_text = '\n'.join(s for i in sorted(unrelated) for s in leaves(entries[i], []))
out_text = '\n'.join(s for l in out_lines for s in leaves(json.loads(l), []))
rel_text = '\n'.join(s for i, e in enumerate(entries) if i not in unrelated for s in leaves(e, []))
print(f'unrelated entries: {len(unrelated)}; text {len(un_text)/1e6:.2f} MB; related native {len(rel_text)/1e6:.2f} MB; staged {len(out_text)/1e6:.2f} MB')
un, out, rel = tokens(un_text), tokens(out_text), tokens(rel_text)
rows = []
for tok, n in un.items():
    if n < 4 or out.get(tok, 0) == 0: continue
    r = rel.get(tok, 0)
    ratio = n / (r + 1)
    if ratio >= 1.5: rows.append((ratio, tok, n, r, out[tok]))
rows.sort(reverse=True)
print(f'{len(rows)} tokens are more frequent in the withheld entries than elsewhere and still occur in the staged file')
print('ratio   token                     withheld  related-native  staged')
for ratio, tok, n, r, o in rows[:int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 200]:
    print(f'{ratio:6.1f}  {tok:24}  {n:7}  {r:7}  {o:7}')
EOF

content.content:
--- summary:
Most of the last changes hold up. I reproduced two problems the changes introduced and two pre-existing ones next to them.

What holds:
(a) assertFilesWritable: every case I tried as user nobody and as root under setpriv, with both drivers, behaves as described. The refused cases are a read-only file, a read-only -wal, a read-only -shm, a read-only directory with no side files, a read-only directory with only a -wal, and a symlink to a read-only file. Each one prints one line, exits with code 1 within 0.1-0.9 s, and leaves the directory unchanged (file list, sizes, sha256 and modes). Healthy cases start: side files present in a read-only directory, a group-writable database with side files from a root server already running, symlinks (including link and target in different directories), and new databases. 20x each of generate:east, db:reset and a second server against a database a server holds open, plus 20 pairs of servers started together on a new file, were never refused.
(b) npm scripts: arguments, including ones with spaces, arrive unchanged; relative and absolute paths resolve from the directory the command is typed in; nothing lands outside .gitignore. "npm start" on a fresh copy works on Node 20, 22 and 24, and the lockfile is byte-identical afterwards.
(c) dev.mjs: normal start works with HOST unset, 127.0.0.1 and 192.0.2.2, and /api is proxied. A first start with PORT=abc, a taken port, a read-only DB or LOG_REQUESTS=2 gives one line, exit 1, no process left and 5173 free. Without node_modules it gives one line. Ctrl+C on a running dev server leaves nothing. A syntax error while editing does not end the command.
(d) The suite gives 191/253 with 0 skipped on Node 22, 20 and 24 from a root-only path (setpriv is used). It gives 191 on SQLITE_DRIVER=node and better-sqlite3, and 191 as user nobody from a copy below /tmp. With setpriv off PATH it gives an honest but vague skip from the root-only path and the nobody fallback from /tmp.

What does not hold:
1. Introduced by the change: the pre-check has a race. When another process closes the database as the last connection while this one starts, assertFilesWritable refuses a healthy, writable database and says a side file is "read-only for this user". It happened 7 times in 40,000 opens, even as root.
2. Introduced by the change: a Ctrl+C at the moment the API comes up leaves an orphaned Vite (parent PID 1) holding port 5173. It happened 2 times in 62 timed tries. The cause is that Vite is now started lazily and passOn() never checks `stopping`.
3. Pre-existing: SIGTERM sent to the `npm run dev` (or `npm start`) process itself leaves dev.mjs, node --watch, the server and Vite running. npm's `sh -c` does not pass the signal on.

---
## 10. Known defects and unfinished work

**Known defects** - behaviour that is wrong or surprising, and that I know of:

- *A very large bulk issue holds every other request up while it runs.* It is one synchronous
  transaction. Measured: issuing to 20,000 eligible learners takes about one second, and a list
  request sent meanwhile waits that long. At the sizes of the specification (a course roster) this
  is milliseconds.
- *List requests are linear in the tenant's size where the export is not.* The substring search of
  a list request, and its deep pages (`page=4000`), scan the tenant's rows in one piece: tens of
  milliseconds at 100,000 certificates, during which other requests wait.
- *A double click on text in a list row opens the certificate instead of selecting the word.* A
  click on a row opens the drawer at once; selecting by dragging works, and the same text can be
  selected in the drawer.
- *Leaving with the browser's Back button while a revocation is on its way* closes the
  confirmation without its outcome message. The request is not cancelled; the list shows the result.
- *A download cut short is not noticed by every client.* The server resets the connection of a
  download it gives up, but netcat and raw Node.js sockets report a reset after data as a normal
  end; and a client that half-closes its connection (`nc -N`) or reads more slowly than a few kB/s
  for five minutes is treated as gone (see *Export without blocking* in section 7).
- *Idempotency keys are kept for ever.* Nothing expires them, so the table grows by one row per
  bulk issue.
- *After a refused `npm run db:reset` on a read-only database* the message ends with a hint about
  damaged files that does not apply to that case.

**Not verified** - I have no evidence either way:

- Browsers other than Chromium, and real screen readers. Keyboard operation, focus handling and the
  accessibility tree were checked in Chromium only.
- Windows. The commands and tests were run on Linux (Node 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22).
- More than 100,000 certificates per tenant (the generator accepts up to 2,000,000).

**Unfinished work** - not built, and what I would do next:

- *Excluded by the specification:* real authentication and authorisation (the actor header is
  trusted as it is), deployment, notifications.
- *Management of tenants, admins, courses, learners and enrollments.* They exist only as seeded
  demo data; the console reads them.
- *Very large bulk issues as a background job* with progress, instead of one request.
- *Keyset pagination and a search index* (trigram or full-text) for tenants far beyond 10⁵
  certificates.
- *Re-issuing after a revocation.* Today a learner whose certificate was revoked is skipped with
  the reason `certificate_revoked`; whether and how to issue again is a policy decision.
- *Changing a tenant's time zone.* The local issue date is stored with each certificate and would
  have to be recomputed.
- *Browser tests in the repository.* The UI tests run the real application in a simulated DOM
  against recorded API answers; the checks in a real browser were done with throw-away scripts
  that are not part of the repository.
- *Continuous integration.* `npm test` is the whole verification; nothing runs it automatically.

---

### Reproducing A1–A7 by hand

`npm test` checks all of this automatically. The steps below show each criterion on the running
app instead: start it as in section 1, then use a second terminal (POSIX shell with `curl`;
`node` prints one JSON answer readably). They begin with the quick-start data and are meant to be
run in this order - A3 and A4 use the answers of A2.

```bash
npm run db:reset
A='X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test'; B='X-Actor-Email: bob@west.test'
URL=http://localhost:3000; J='Content-Type: application/json'
```

**A1 – tenant isolation.**

```bash
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates" | grep -o '"serialNumber":"[A-Z]*' | sort | uniq -c   # 7 x EAST
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates" | grep -o '"serialNumber":"[A-Z]*' | sort | uniq -c   # 4 x WEST
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\n' -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/1"        # East's certificate as West: 404 ...
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\n' -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/999999"   # ... word for word the answer for an id that does not exist
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\n' -X POST -H "$B" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: a1' \
     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                          # East's course as West: 404 "Course not found"
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?pageSize=1" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # East still has 7 certificates,
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/audit-events"            | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # 8 audit events
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                                          # and no operation: {"items":[]}
```

In the UI: act as Bob and open `http://localhost:3000/#/certificates/1` - *Certificate not found*.

**A2 – one key is one operation, sequentially and concurrently.**

```bash
for i in 1 2 3; do            # sequential: executed once, then the stored answer
  curl -s -i -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-seq' -d '{"courseId": 2}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" \
    | grep -iE '^HTTP|^idempotent-replayed'
done                          # 201 + "Idempotent-Replayed: false", then twice 201 + "true"

seq 20 | xargs -P 20 -I{} curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' \
     -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" -o /tmp/a2-{}.json        # 20 requests at once, one key
sort -u /tmp/a2-*.json | wc -l                                                    # 1: all twenty answers are the same
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues" | grep -o '"id":[0-9]*,"status"' | wc -l   # 2 operations, one per key
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?pageSize=1" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'     # 10 certificates: 7 + 1 + 2
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/audit-events?action=certificate.issued" | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'   # 10: one issue event each
```

**A3 – the same key with another payload.**

```bash
curl -s -w ' -> %{http_code}\n' -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' \
     -d '{"courseId": 3}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues"                           # 409 idempotency_key_reused
curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -H 'Idempotency-Key: demo-par' -d '{"courseId": 1}' "$URL/api/bulk-issues" \
  | cmp - /tmp/a2-1.json && echo 'first result intact'                    # the original request still gets the first answer
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/bulk-issues" | grep -o '"id":[0-9]*,"status"' | wc -l   # still 2 operations
```

**A4 – the outcome of every learner.**

```bash
node -e 'const o = require("/tmp/a2-1.json"); console.log(o.summary);
  for (const r of o.results) console.log(r.learnerName.padEnd(16), r.outcome, r.reason ?? "", r.serialNumber ?? "")'
# { total: 5, issued: 2, skipped: 3, failed: 0 }
# Alex Lee         skipped already_certified EAST-0000001
# Marcus O'Connor  issued  EAST-0000009
# Mei Chen         skipped not_completed
# Priya Sharma     issued  EAST-0000010
# Tom Walker       skipped not_completed
```

A `failed` outcome needs a write that goes wrong for one learner, which cannot be provoked from
outside; the tests do it by injecting the fault (`acceptance.test.js` › *bulk issue with injected
failures*). The Bulk issue page shows the same outcomes, with the reasons in words.

**A5 – tenant-local dates.**

```bash
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/1" | grep -o '"issuedAt":"[^"]*","issuedLocal":"[^"]*"'   # 2026-01-10T13:30:00.000Z -> 2026-01-11 00:30
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/8" | grep -o '"issuedAt":"[^"]*","issuedLocal":"[^"]*"'   # the same instant -> 2026-01-10 21:30
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc" | head -3   # ordered and printed by the Sydney date
curl -s -H "$B" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc" | head -3   # ... and by the Perth date
```

**A6 – 100,000 certificates.**

```bash
npm run generate:east                           # about 3 s; the server keeps running
Q='q=an&sort=learner&order=desc'
time curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?$Q" -o /tmp/e1.csv   # well under a second each
time curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv?$Q" -o /tmp/e2.csv
cmp /tmp/e1.csv /tmp/e2.csv && wc -l < /tmp/e1.csv                          # identical; 25,481 lines (header + 25,480 rows)

# equal sort keys come in id order (most rows of this page share their name with the row before):
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?sort=learner&order=asc&pageSize=100&page=7" | node -e '
  const { items } = JSON.parse(require("fs").readFileSync(0));
  const inOrder = items.every((c, i) => i === 0 || c.learnerName !== items[i - 1].learnerName || c.id > items[i - 1].id);
  console.log(inOrder ? "ties in ascending id order" : "NOT in id order")'

# list requests are answered (in milliseconds) while three full exports are streaming:
for i in 1 2 3; do curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/export.csv" -o /dev/null & done
for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}s ' -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates?page=40&pageSize=50"; done; echo; wait

npm run generate:east -- --clear                # back to the quick-start certificates
```

**A7 – revocation and its audit event.**

```bash
curl -s -X POST -H "$A" -H "$J" -d '{"reason":"Issued in error"}' "$URL/api/certificates/3/revoke" \
  | grep -o '"alreadyRevoked":[a-z]*'                                              # false: revoked by this request
curl -s -X POST -H "$A" "$URL/api/certificates/3/revoke" | grep -o '"alreadyRevoked":[a-z]*'   # true: nothing changes
curl -s -H "$A" "$URL/api/audit-events?certificateId=3" | grep -o '"action":"[a-z.]*"' | sort | uniq -c
#   1 "action":"certificate.issued"
#   1 "action":"certificate.revoked"
```

In the UI: open a certificate, *Revoke certificate…*, confirm; the audit trail in the drawer shows
the new event. `npm run db:reset` restores the quick-start data afterwards.

by `frontend/test`: the real application is mounted in a simulated browser and talks to a fake

with `node frontend/test/fixtures/record.mjs` after changing the API).

with other work they are several times larger): filtered and sorted exports of 10,000–100,000
rows take 0.2–0.3 s each and are byte-identical across runs; while three full 100,000-row exports
stream concurrently, some 500 list requests are answered with a median of 4 ms and a worst case

# Certificate Admin Console

Internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform. Tenant admins review course
completions, bulk-issue certificates, revoke them, and export certificate data as CSV.

| Layer    | Stack                                                                    |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Backend  | Node.js, Express 5, SQLite (file database in WAL mode, persistent)       |
| Frontend | React 19, Vite                                                           |
| Tests    | API: `node:test`, black-box over HTTP against the real server process. UI: Vitest + Testing Library, the real app against recorded API answers |

**Requirements:** Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ (any newer release works as well) with npm. Nothing
else to install. Verified on Node 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22.

**Where to find what:**

| | |
| --- | --- |
| One-command start, verification command | [1. Run it](#1-run-it): `npm start`, `npm test` |
| Actors (request header, no login) | [2. Actors and demo data](#2-actors-and-demo-data): `X-Actor-Email` |
| Demo data | created by the first start; described in [section 2](#2-actors-and-demo-data) |
| 100,000 certificates for East | [4. Load-test data](#4-load-test-data-100000-certificates): `npm run generate:east` |
| A1–A7: how each is met, and how to reproduce it | [6. How the acceptance criteria are met](#6-how-the-acceptance-criteria-are-met), [Reproducing A1–A7 by hand](#reproducing-a1a7-by-hand) |
| Known defects, unfinished work | [10. Known defects and unfinished work](#10-known-defects-and-unfinished-work) |

![Certificate list](docs/screenshots/01-certificates.png)

---

## 1. Run it

```bash
npm start
```

That one command installs the declared dependencies, builds the UI, creates the SQLite database
with the demo data (first run only) and starts the whole app on **http://localhost:3000**.

```bash
npm test
```

Runs the verification suite: 191 API tests covering acceptance criteria A1–A7, including the
100,000-row export checks, followed by 253 UI tests of the four workflows. It uses throw-away
databases in the OS temp directory and never touches the app's data. Takes about a minute. (One
API test needs a file the server may read but not write. Root may write every file, so when the
suite runs as root - in a container, say - that test starts its server without that one privilege
(with `setpriv`) or, failing that, as the unprivileged user `nobody`; where neither is possible
it is reported as skipped, with the reason.)

Other commands:

| Command                               | What it does                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run generate:east`               | Adds 100,000 certificates to tenant East (see [section 4](#4-load-test-data-100000-certificates)) |
| `npm run generate:east -- --clear`    | Removes the generated certificates again                                     |
| `npm run db:reset`                    | Restores the pristine quick-start dataset (safe while the server is running) |
| `PORT=4000 npm start`                 | Use another port (more settings below)                                       |
| `npm run dev`                         | Development mode: API with auto-restart + Vite dev server on :5173           |

`npm start` and `npm test` install what they need. The other commands rely on that having happened
once - `npm run dev` says so in one line if it has not. Data lives in `data/cert-admin.sqlite` and
survives restarts.

Settings, all optional, are environment variables; one that is set but blank (empty, or nothing
but white space) counts as not set, and numbers are written in plain decimal digits. A value that
cannot be used is reported in one line and nothing starts: the settings are checked first, then
the port is claimed, and only then is the database opened (or created) - a start that fails on a
setting or on the port does not leave a database file behind. A database that cannot be written
to (a read-only file or directory) is refused at that point as well, not at the first write, and
is left exactly as it was found. The line printed after a successful start names the address to
open: `localhost` when the server listens on all interfaces, the configured `HOST` otherwise.

| Variable                 | Default                  | Meaning |
| ------------------------ | ------------------------ | ------- |
| `PORT`                   | `3000`                   | HTTP port |
| `HOST`                   | all interfaces           | Address to listen on (`127.0.0.1` = this machine only) |
| `DB_PATH`                | `data/cert-admin.sqlite` | Database file |
| `STATIC_DIR`             | `frontend/dist`          | Directory with the built UI that the server serves (`npm start` builds it there) |
| `LOG_REQUESTS`           | `1` (on)                 | `0` turns the request log off |
| `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`     | `10000`                  | How long a write waits for another process's write lock before answering 503 |
| `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT`  | `4`                      | CSV exports that read at the same time; further ones wait their turn |
| `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` | `300000`                 | A download that makes no progress for this long is dropped (`0` = never) |
| `SQLITE_DRIVER`          | automatic                | `better-sqlite3` or `node` to force one of the two drivers |

A relative path - in `DB_PATH`, `STATIC_DIR` or after `--db` - is taken from the directory the
command is typed in.

The examples in this README are written for a POSIX shell (macOS, Linux, Git Bash or WSL on
Windows). In PowerShell set a variable first, for example `$env:PORT=4000; npm start`; the `npm`
commands themselves are the same everywhere.

## 2. Actors and demo data

There is no login. Every request names its actor in the **`X-Actor-Email`** header; the server looks
the admin up and derives the tenant from that record. The tenant is never read from the URL, the
query string or the body. In the UI, use the **Acting as** switcher in the top-right corner.

| Actor             | Tenant | Time zone          | Serial prefix |
| ----------------- | ------ | ------------------ | ------------- |

## 9. Troubleshooting

- **Port 3000 is in use** – the server says so and exits; start it with `PORT=4000 npm start`.
- **Want a clean slate** – `npm run db:reset`. It empties and re-seeds the tables in one
  transaction, so it works while the server runs (the server simply serves the fresh data
  afterwards). If it reports that the database is busy, another process is in the middle of a
  write (for example the generator): nothing was changed, run it again in a moment.
- **"Database schema version … is not supported"** – the database file was created by a different
  version of this app. Stop the server and run `npm run db:reset`, which recreates the file.
- **A request answers `503 database_busy`** – another process held the write lock for more than
  10 seconds. Nothing was written; repeat the request (the UI offers *Retry safely*), or raise
  the limit with `DB_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS=60000 npm start`.
- **An export answers `503 export_busy`** – four exports are running and 32 more are waiting.
  Try again in a few seconds, or raise `EXPORT_MAX_CONCURRENT` (the exports then share the server
  among more of them; other requests are not slowed down by that).
- **A very slow download breaks off** – a download that makes no progress for 5 minutes is
  disconnected so that it cannot hold a database snapshot open indefinitely. A client that reads
  steadily but very slowly (a few kB/s on a fast local connection) can look like that to the server,
  see *Export without blocking* above; raise `EXPORT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` (or set it to `0`).
- **`npm warn deprecated prebuild-install…` during the first install** – harmless; it comes from
  the installer of the optional native SQLite module.
- **`package-lock.json` and `.npmrc`** – the lockfile pins the exact dependency versions, and
  `npm start` leaves it untouched. `.npmrc` sets `legacy-peer-deps` for one reason: without it
  npm 10.9 (the npm of Node 22) cannot work out the dependency tree when the lockfile is missing
  and stops with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')`. With the lockfile in
  place the setting changes nothing.
- **"…was installed with another Node.js version"** – the native SQLite module is built for one
  Node.js version. After switching versions run `npm rebuild better-sqlite3` (the message says so),

然后这个是我对于作业的第六章的回答：1. Column Migration & Rollback
Why it fails: During a rolling deployment, old and new versions run at the same time. If you drop `display_name` too early, old instances crash because the column is missing. If you switch reads/writes to `full_name` before creating it, new instances crash. You also lose data and can't safely roll back once `display_name` is dropped.
Safe sequence:

1. Add `full_name` as nullable in the database.
2. Deploy code that writes to both `display_name` and `full_name`, while still reading from `display_name`.
3. Backfill existing `display_name` values into `full_name` in small batches.
4. Deploy code that reads from `full_name` (falling back to `display_name` if null) while keeping dual-writes on.
5. Once confident and no rollback is needed, stop writing to `display_name`.
6. In a later release, drop `display_name`.

2. Stale Cache After Revocation
Why a 5-second TTL doesn't fix it: It doesn't remove the race condition—it just shrinks the window where bad data is served. Even for 5 seconds, a revoked certificate could still look `ACTIVE` to callers, which is a security bug.
How to fix it:

* Version check (best): Give each certificate a monotonically increasing `version` number. When B revokes it, bump the version in the DB and write a `REVOKED` entry (or tombstone) with that new version to the cache. When A tries to write back to the cache, only let the write succeed if A's version is newer than what's already in the cache.
* Locking alternative: Use a per-certificate lock around cache updates/deletes so A's read-and-populate and B's revoke-and-invalidate can't interleave out of order.

3. Cascading Failure & Recovery
Chain of failure: Normally, 1,000 req/s at 20 ms takes about 20 workers. When B slows to 2 seconds, requests hit the 100 ms timeout and retry up to 3 times—turning 1,000 req/s into up to 4,000 calls against B and holding each request open longer. All 50 workers on A get tied up waiting on `/report`, starving every other endpoint on A.
How to fix `/report`:

* Isolate resources: Cap how many workers `/report` (or calls to B) can use at once so other endpoints still have free workers.
* Add a circuit breaker: If B times out or errors too often, trip the circuit breaker and fail fast without calling B until it recovers.
* Cut back retries: Drop aggressive retries when B is struggling (or use a tight retry budget) so you don't flood a slow service.

What `/report` should return when B is unhealthy: Return a fast degraded response—like a cached report if you have one (ideally marked stale), or a quick `503 Service Unavailable` with a `Retry-After` header (or `202 Accepted` if queued for async processing).  然后他的题目是：Answer all three questions in written-answers.md , in your own words.

this release can fail and propose a safe sequence of database and application changes.
2. Certificate details are cached for 60 seconds. Request A misses the cache and reads ACTIVE
from the database. Before A writes to the cache, request B revokes the certificate, commits
the database transaction, and deletes the cache entry. A then writes its stale ACTIVE value
into the cache. A colleague proposes reducing the cache TTL to five seconds. Explain why this

second. B's latency suddenly rises from 20 ms to 2 seconds, and unrelated endpoints on A
soon stop responding. Explain the chain of failure, including the effect of retries. Redesign

# Written answers

## 1. Column Migration & Rollback

Why it fails: During a rolling deployment, old and new versions run at the same time. If you drop `display_name` too early, old instances crash because the column is missing. If you switch reads/writes to `full_name` before creating it, new instances crash. You also lose data and can't safely roll back once `display_name` is dropped.

Safe sequence:

1. Add `full_name` as nullable in the database.
2. Deploy code that writes to both `display_name` and `full_name`, while still reading from `display_name`.
3. Backfill existing `display_name` values into `full_name` in small batches.
4. Deploy code that reads from `full_name` (falling back to `display_name` if null) while keeping dual-writes on.
5. Once confident and no rollback is needed, stop writing to `display_name`.
6. In a later release, drop `display_name`.

## 2. Stale Cache After Revocation

Why a 5-second TTL doesn't fix it: It doesn't remove the race condition—it just shrinks the window where bad data is served. Even for 5 seconds, a revoked certificate could still look `ACTIVE` to callers, which is a security bug.

How to fix it:

* Version check (best): Give each certificate a monotonically increasing `version` number. When B revokes it, bump the version in the DB and write a `REVOKED` entry (or tombstone) with that new version to the cache. When A tries to write back to the cache, only let the write succeed if A's version is newer than what's already in the cache.
* Locking alternative: Use a per-certificate lock around cache updates/deletes so A's read-and-populate and B's revoke-and-invalidate can't interleave out of order.

## 3. Cascading Failure & Recovery

Chain of failure: Normally, 1,000 req/s at 20 ms takes about 20 workers. When B slows to 2 seconds, requests hit the 100 ms timeout and retry up to 3 times—turning 1,000 req/s into up to 4,000 calls against B and holding each request open longer. All 50 workers on A get tied up waiting on `/report`, starving every other endpoint on A.

How to fix `/report`:

* Isolate resources: Cap how many workers `/report` (or calls to B) can use at once so other endpoints still have free workers.
* Add a circuit breaker: If B times out or errors too often, trip the circuit breaker and fail fast without calling B until it recovers.
* Cut back retries: Drop aggressive retries when B is struggling (or use a tight retry budget) so you don't flood a slow service.

What `/report` should return when B is unhealthy: Return a fast degraded response—like a cached report if you have one (ideally marked stale), or a quick `503 Service Unavailable` with a `Retry-After` header (or `202 Accepted` if queued for async processing).

```bash
npm run generate:east
```
