file.content:
# AI interaction evidence

This directory documents how AI was used for this assignment.

One AI tool was used: **Claude Code** (Anthropic), as a cloud session at claude.ai/code (the
candidate confirms this in the [completeness declaration](completeness-declaration.md)).
Everything - planning, code, tests, verification, the README, the git history and this evidence -
happened in **one interactive session**. For the assignment that session started
**@@SUBAGENTS@@ sub-agent sessions**, in @@RUNS@@ runs: to have its work checked by sessions that had not written
it, in one run to rework the UI, and in the last two runs to review this evidence. (Six more sub-agent
sessions, in two runs, belong to an unrelated request and are not exported; see below.)

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl`](sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl) | The interactive session: the tool's own transcript file, JSON Lines, one entry per line - prompts, assistant messages, tool calls with their inputs (commands, file edits), tool results and errors, each with its time. Changed only where the table of replacements below says so. |
| [`sessions/readable/`](sessions/readable/README.md) | The same session as text for reading, in parts. Generated from the `.jsonl`; long tool inputs and outputs are shortened there. |
| [`sessions/subagents/`](sessions/subagents/README.md) | The sub-agent sessions: one compressed JSON Lines file each (`zcat agent-<id>.jsonl.gz`) with the tool's note on it (`agent-<id>.meta.json`), plus, per run, the tool's record of the run with every returned result (`run.json`), its journal and the script the main session wrote for it (`script.js`). The README there says what each run was for and how each sub-agent ended. |
| [`sessions/tool-results/`](sessions/tool-results/) | Tool outputs that were too long for the transcript: the tool keeps them in files of their own, and the sessions name them. (Copied for everything up to line 5200 and for the sub-agents; the long outputs of the commands that prepared this export are not.) |
| [`sessions/redaction-report.json`](sessions/redaction-report.json) | How many replacements were made, by reason, and which lines of the interactive session are withheld. |
| [`session-index.csv`](session-index.csv) | One row per session: `session_id, tool, model, started_at, ended_at, export_file, purpose, related_commits`. All times are UTC. For the interactive session `ended_at` is the time of its last exported line (the completeness declaration says what follows it). The six sessions that are not exported have a row each, without a file. |
| [`tool-actions.csv`](tool-actions.csv) | Tool action evidence: every tool call of every session in the order of the clock - the command that was run or the file that was edited, by which session, with what result - with the line of the session file that holds it. Generated from the session files. |
| [`decision-log.md`](decision-log.md) | Material decisions, each linked to the session lines, the verification evidence and the commits. |
| [`completeness-declaration.md`](completeness-declaration.md) | Tools used, limitations of the export, and the candidate's confirmations. |
| [`export/`](export/) | The two scripts that produced the files above from the tool's transcript files, and the description of the runs they use. |

**AI instruction files.** The project has none: no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, rules or prompt files
were written or used, and the repository has never contained one. What the assistant was told is
in the session itself: everything the candidate typed (marked "candidate" in the reading copy and
listed in the decision log), and the instructions the main session wrote for its sub-agents
(`script.js` of each run). Two things came from the tool, not from the candidate: the reference
text of its workflow feature (the tool put it into the conversation at lines 533 and 1524 - the
second time because the assistant asked for it at line 1522 - and attached it again after each
compaction; withheld as vendor material), and the tool's notice of its workflow mode (from
line 531 on).

## How the export was made

The tool keeps a transcript file per session on the machine the session runs on
(`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session id>.jsonl`, and one file per sub-agent below
`<session id>/subagents/`). [`export/export_sessions.py`](export/export_sessions.py) copies those
files line by line and changes a line only where one of the rules below applies. Every change
leaves `[REDACTED: reason]` in place of what was removed, so position, kind and size of the removed
text stay visible. Where more than a text goes, the marker stands for the whole value: a withheld
tool input becomes `{"redacted": "[REDACTED: …]"}`, an attachment of the tool its type and one
marker, any other object or list one marker string. Empty values stay empty.
[`export/build_indexes.py`](export/build_indexes.py) then builds the two CSV files and the reading
copy from the exported files alone.

The exporter reads the private terms and the numbers of the withheld lines from a configuration
file that is not published: it consists of the very terms that are withheld. Its settings are the
line ranges of the unrelated request, the patterns of private terms and names, the letters for
the model names, and the reasons printed in the markers. The line ranges are in
`sessions/redaction-report.json`; the reasons are the ones in the tables below.

The line numbers used everywhere (decision log, reading copy, `tool-actions.csv`) are the lines of
the exported file, which are the lines of the tool's file: no line is added, dropped or moved.

Run from the root of the repository:

```bash
# the candidate's prompts, in order, and the messages sent while the assistant was working
# (other kinds of entries hold the rest of what the candidate typed: the two messages that were
# never delivered, lines 5410 and 6372; the command at line 516; the answers at line 6368 -
# the table in decision-log.md lists everything)
jq -r 'if .type == "user" and .origin.kind == "human" and (.message.content | type) == "string"
       then "\(.timestamp)  \(.message.content[0:100] | gsub("\n"; " "))"
       elif .type == "attachment" and .attachment.type == "queued_command" and (.attachment.prompt | startswith("<") | not)
       then "\(.timestamp)  \(.attachment.prompt[0:100] | gsub("\n"; " "))"
       else empty end' ai/sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl
# every command the assistant ran
jq -r 'select(.type == "assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type == "tool_use" and .name == "Bash")
       | .input.command // .input.redacted' ai/sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl
# one line of the file (the decision log refers to lines)
sed -n '5396p' ai/sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl | jq .
```

## What was replaced, and why

**Another request in the same session.** During the session the candidate also asked the
assistant for something that has nothing to do with the assignment (line 554; the request itself
is kept as typed). The assistant's work on it dealt with private documents about third parties.

| Marker | What it stands for |
| --- | --- |
| `unrelated private request handled in the same session - third-party business documents` | What the entries of that work say: lines @@WITHHELD_RANGES@@. Every entry is still there, with its kind and its time. |
| `notice of the tool about background work of the unrelated private request` | The tool's notices that background work of that request had ended; they quote its results. (These are entries of the tool, not prompts of the candidate.) |
| `line that refers to the unrelated private request` | Later mentions of that request in messages, notes and summaries: the sentence or line that mentions it, and list items below it. |
| `file …`, `directory …`, `job name …`, `tool name of the unrelated request`, `private term` | Names of its files, directories, jobs and connector tools, wherever they occur; single terms inside two commands that are otherwise kept (lines 5470 and 5474). |
| `tool output that shows material of the unrelated private request`, `text shown while this export was prepared that repeats words of the unrelated private request` | From line 5200 on the session built and checked this export. Commands that handled the private terms, outputs that print several lines naming the request, and outputs that repeat a passage of the withheld text are replaced as a whole. |
| `working step of a session that reviewed this export and was given its files, the withheld material included`, `result of a review of this export: it describes the withheld material to say where traces of it were found` | The nine sub-agents of the last two runs (`wf_ce880d66-b3c`, `wf_64f4f895-96e`) reviewed this export; some compared it with the original transcript. Of their sessions the task is exported. What they typed into tools, what the tools answered, their notes on the way and the text of their results are replaced: a review that looks for traces of private material has to describe that material. How many findings each returned, and how severe, is in the marker; what was changed because of them is in decision 6 of the decision log. |

Two sub-agent runs that belong to that request (`wf_34e04759-afc` and `wf_7ccfb441-20f`, six
sessions) are not exported at all.

**Personal data.**

| Marker | What it stands for |
| --- | --- |
| `candidate e-mail address`, `account identifier` | The candidate's e-mail address and two identifiers of the account. |
| `list of the candidate's other repositories - unrelated to this assignment`, `another repository of the candidate`, `name of an organisation of the candidate's account` | What the candidate's GitHub account holds besides this repository. |
| `e-mail address of the assignment's reviewer`, `name of the assignment's reviewer`, `name of the company that set the assignment` | The person the submission is sent to, and the company. They occur in the candidate's prompts where the assignment's text is quoted. Replaced because this repository is public. |

**Material of the tool's vendor, and binary data.**

| Marker | What it stands for |
| --- | --- |
| `built-in system prompt and tool definitions of the AI tool (vendor material)`, `definitions of tools …`, `documentation page of the AI tool …`, `bundled reference text of the AI tool …` | What the tool itself puts in front of the conversation or hands to the assistant on request: its system prompt, the definitions of its tools, a page of its documentation, the reference text of its workflow feature. |
| `reminder or instruction text of the AI tool (vendor material)` | The text the tool renders from its reminders (environment description, mode notices) for the model. The structured part of each such entry is kept. |
| `catalogue of tools and connectors … / of skills … available in the account`, `instructions of the connectors …`, `catalogue of agent types …` | Lists of what is installed in the candidate's account. |
| `binary data (base64), …` | Screenshots the assistant took of the running app and looked at. Size and a checksum are in the marker; the three screenshots used in the README are in `docs/screenshots/`. |
| `opaque signature of a reasoning block, …` | A signature the tool stores with each reasoning step of the model (see the limitations in the declaration). |
| `model identifier A` … `E` | The names of AI models, wherever they occur: see the next section. |

Kept on purpose: the short notices with which the tool marks events in the conversation (a
background task has ended, a message arrived while the assistant was working, the conversation
was compacted, the model was changed) - they are part of what happened; and the name of the
candidate's GitHub account, which owns this public repository.

Nothing else was changed. About @@IDENTICAL_PCT@@ % of the lines of the interactive session are byte for byte
the tool's lines. Most of the others differ only in a model identifier, a reasoning signature or a
reminder text of the tool; `sessions/redaction-report.json` has the counts (they count
replacements made by the export: a later command that prints a marker is not counted again).

## Model identifiers

The tool records the model with every assistant entry. In these files the names are replaced by
letters, consistently, so that it stays visible which model did what:

- **A** - the model named in the `Co-Authored-By` line of this repository's commits. It wrote all of
  the main session after its first minutes, and ran the sub-agents of the first five runs.
- **B** - another model of the same vendor. It produced the first four assistant entries of the
  main session (lines 21, 22, 29 and 30; the last one at 07:18:33 UTC). The candidate switched to
  model A with the tool's `/model` command: the command carries the time 07:09:28 and is stored
  further down, at lines 516 and 518, out of time order. Every assistant entry written by a model from line 34
  (07:19:09) on carries A. Model B also ran the sub-agents of the later runs (verification
  round 4, the confirmation run, the two reviews of this evidence): the main session named it in the
  scripts of those runs. Before that, the usage limit of model A had cut two runs short (lines
  944 and 3525); the limit notices say so, the session gives no other reason for the choice.
- **C, D, E** - further model names that are only mentioned in text.

The reason for the letters, as the assistant states it (line 6365): it works under a rule of its
tool not to write model identifiers into files that are pushed to a repository; the co-author line
of the commits is where the tool itself names the model. The text of that rule belongs to the
tool's own prompt material, which is withheld, so the statement cannot be checked from this
export. **This departs from section 5 of the assignment**, which asks for model identifiers where
the tool records them, and model B is not named anywhere in this repository. The candidate was
asked and chose to leave the letters in place (line 6368).

## Limitations of this export

They are listed, with the candidate's confirmations, in
[`completeness-declaration.md`](completeness-declaration.md).

569	def inline_terms(node, rules):
570	    """Replace the private terms inside a structure's strings, and nothing around them."""
571	    if isinstance(node, str):
572	        marker = mark('private term')
573	        for rx, replacement in rules.tokens:
574	            node, m = rx.subn(replacement, node)
575	            rules.counts[replacement] += m
576	        node, n = rules.keyword_text.subn(marker, node)
577	        rules.counts[marker] += n
578	        return node
579	    if isinstance(node, list):
580	        return [inline_terms(item, rules) for item in node]
581	    if isinstance(node, dict):
582	        return {key: inline_terms(value, rules) for key, value in node.items()}
583	    return node

599	                    if index in unrelated:

601	    markers = config.get('unrelated_markers', [])
602	    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):

612	        if markers:

638	def export_main(config, rules, out_dir):
639	    with open(config['session_file'], encoding='utf-8') as handle:
640	        lines = [line.rstrip('\n') for line in handle if line.strip()]
641	    limit = config.get('last_line')
642	    if limit:
643	        lines = lines[:limit]
644	    entries = [json.loads(line) for line in lines]
645	    unrelated, call_names = classify_main(entries, config)
646	    withheld_lines = set(config.get('prep_withheld_lines', []))
647	    withheld_calls = {part.get('id') for number, entry in enumerate(entries, 1) if number in withheld_lines and entry.get('type') == 'assistant'
648	                      for part in (entry.get('message') or {}).get('content') or [] if isinstance(part, dict) and part.get('type') == 'tool_use'}
649	    verbatim = set(config.get('verbatim_entries', []))
650	    reason = config['reason_unrelated']
651	    report = collections.Counter()
652	    prep_start = config.get('prep_start')
653	    baseline, quotes, taken = set(), None, 0
654	    withheld_numbers = []
655	    name = f"{config['session_id']}.jsonl"
656	    path = os.path.join(out_dir, name)
657	    with open(path, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as handle:
658	        for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
659	            original = dump(entry)
660	            if index in verbatim:
661	                # The request itself, in the candidate's words: kept as typed.
662	                result = named_only(rules.binary(copy.deepcopy(entry)), rules)
663	            elif index in unrelated:

665	            elif prep_start is not None and index >= prep_start:
666	                rules.prep = True

670	                quotes |= grams_of('\n'.join(rules.withheld_lines[taken:]), collections.Counter()) - baseline
671	                taken = seen
672	                result = redact_related(copy.deepcopy(entry), rules, call_names, index, quotes, withheld_calls=withheld_calls)
673	            else:
674	                result = redact_related(copy.deepcopy(entry), rules, call_names, index)
675	                if prep_start is not None:
676	                    baseline |= grams_of('\n'.join(strings_of(result)), collections.Counter())
677	            text = dump(result)
678	            if index in unrelated and index not in verbatim:
679	                withheld_numbers.append(index + 1)  # also the tool's own bookkeeping lines in between, which carry no text
680	            if text == original:
681	                report['lines identical to the tool\'s file'] += 1

704	            last = number

717	def findings_note(result):
718	    """'14 findings: 1 blocker, 5 major, ...' for a review result, so that its size stays visible."""

736	def working_withheld(entry, reason, rules):
737	    """A session that handled the withheld material itself: keep its task and what it returned,

739	    if entry.get('type') == 'attachment' and isinstance(entry.get('attachment'), dict):
740	        entry['attachment'] = {'type': entry['attachment'].get('type'), 'redacted': withhold(entry['attachment'], reason, rules)}

743	        return entry
744	    message = entry.get('message')
745	    if not isinstance(message, dict) or not isinstance(message.get('content'), list):
746	        return entry
747	    for part in message['content']:
748	        if not isinstance(part, dict):
749	            continue
750	        if part.get('type') == 'tool_use' and part.get('name') == 'StructuredOutput':
751	            part['input'] = {'redacted': review_result(part.get('input'), rules)}
752	        elif part.get('type') == 'tool_use':
753	            part['input'] = {'redacted': withhold(part.get('input'), reason, rules)}
754	        elif part.get('type') == 'tool_result':

757	            key = part['type']

c = json.load(open('private-config.json', encoding='utf-8'))
# phrases of the tool's own texts that the checks look for: kept in the configuration from now on
c['vendor_phrases'] = ['You are powered by the model', 'Assistant knowledge cutoff', '# userEmail', 'As you answer the user\'s questions, you can use the following context']
c['kept_notice_phrases'] = ['SYSTEM NOTIFICATION - NOT USER INPUT']
json.dump(c, open('private-config.json', 'w', encoding='utf-8'), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1)
s = open('final_checks.py', encoding='utf-8').read()
old_start = s.index("# 3. material of the tool that should be absent")
old_end = s.index("# 4. the words that are private only")
new = '''# 3. material of the tool that should be absent, and notices that are kept on purpose
#    (the phrases are in the configuration; places are counted by the kind of field they sit in)
def fields(node, acc, where=''):
    if isinstance(node, str):
        acc.append((where, node))
    elif isinstance(node, list):
        for item in node:
            fields(item, acc, where + ('[' + str(item.get('type')) + ']' if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get('type') else '[]'))
    elif isinstance(node, dict):
        for key, value in node.items():
            fields(value, acc, where + '.' + key)
    return acc

main_text = next(text for rel, text in texts.items() if rel.endswith(main_name))
for label, phrases in (('sentences of the tool\\'s reminder texts', config.get('vendor_phrases', [])), ('notice texts kept on purpose', config.get('kept_notice_phrases', []))):
    places = collections.Counter()
    for number, line in enumerate(main_text.split('\\n'), 1):
        if not line.strip() or not any(p in line for p in phrases):
            continue
        entry = json.loads(line)
        kind = entry.get('type') + ('/' + str((entry.get('attachment') or {}).get('type')) if entry.get('type') == 'attachment' else '') + ('/summary' if entry.get('isCompactSummary') else '') + ('/meta' if entry.get('isMeta') else '')
        for where, text in fields(entry, []):
            n = sum(text.count(p) for p in phrases)
            if n:
                where = re.sub(r'toolu_\\w+', 'ID', where)
                places[f'{kind} {where}'] += n
    elsewhere = sum(text.count(p) for rel, text in texts.items() if not rel.endswith(main_name) and 'readable/' not in rel for p in phrases)
    print(f'     {label}: {sum(places.values())} in the main session, {elsewhere} in other files (reading copy not counted)')
    for place, n in places.most_common(14):
        print(f'       {n:5d}  {place}')

'''
s = s[:old_start] + new + s[old_end:]
s = s.replace("main_text = next(text for rel, text in texts.items() if rel.endswith(main_name))\nprep = config.get('prep_start') or 10 ** 9", "prep = config.get('prep_start') or 10 ** 9")
open('final_checks.py', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(s)

'''

export const meta = {
  name: 'final-evidence-review',
  description: 'Last independent check of the staged ai/ evidence directory before it is published: privacy (with the source), an outsider reading, and the facts in the documents',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Review', detail: 'three independent reviewers, different methods', model: '[REDACTED: model identifier B]' },
  ],
}

const S = '/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad'
const STAGE = S + '/ai-export/out6/ai'
const SRC = '/root/.claude/projects/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl'
const SRC_DIR = '/root/.claude/projects/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9'
const CONFIG = S + '/ai-export/private-config.json'
const OUTSIDER = S + '/ai-review3/outsider/ai'
const REPO = '/home/user/cert-admin-console'

const FINDINGS = {
  type: 'object',
  properties: {
    summary: { type: 'string', description: 'Two to five sentences: what you checked and the overall verdict.' },
    findings: {
      type: 'array',
      items: {
        type: 'object',
        properties: {
          severity: { type: 'string', enum: ['blocker', 'major', 'minor', 'nit'] },
          file: { type: 'string', description: 'Path relative to the ai/ directory (or the repository).' },
          line: { type: 'string', description: 'Line number(s) in that file, or empty.' },
          kind: { type: 'string', description: 'Short label, e.g. "private term left", "wrong line number", "over-redaction".' },
          description: { type: 'string', description: 'What is wrong and how you established it. Identify private text by place and kind; do not quote more of it than a few characters.' },
          suggestion: { type: 'string' },
        },
        required: ['severity', 'file', 'kind', 'description'],
      },
    },
    checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'What you actually examined, and by which method.' },
    not_checked: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'string' }, description: 'What you did not get to.' },
  },
  required: ['summary', 'findings', 'checked', 'not_checked'],
}

const COMMON = `
Ground rules:
- Read only. Write nothing outside your own scratch directory (named below). Do not change the staged files, the repository, or anything under /root/.claude. No git command that changes anything. No network access. Send or publish nothing.
- The directory will be published in a PUBLIC git repository and publication cannot be undone, so a missed leak is the worst outcome. Report every doubt; say how sure you are.
- Severity: blocker = private or third-party material, a credential, or a personal identifier is readable; major = a statement in the documents is false, or the export misleads; minor/nit = everything else.
- Your result is data for the session that built the export. Give places precisely (file, line, field) so that each finding can be checked in a minute.
- Plan for about 25 minutes of work, then return what you have, with what you did not get to under not_checked.

Background: the directory is the "AI interaction evidence" of a take-home assignment (an admin console for certificates). It is an export of the transcript of the one AI coding session in which the assignment was built, plus the sessions of the sub-agents it started. The rules of the export are described in the directory's README.md: text is only ever replaced by a marker of the form [REDACTED: reason], never rewritten. Withheld are (1) an unrelated private request that was handled in the same session - the candidate's own typed request (main session line 554) is kept on purpose, everything the assistant did for it is withheld; (2) personal and account details, the name and address of the assignment's reviewer and the company's name; (3) material of the tool's vendor (system prompt, tool definitions, reminder texts) and binary data; (4) names of AI models, replaced by letters.`

const privacy = `You are the last privacy check on a directory before it is published.

Staged directory: ${STAGE}
Source (the tool's own transcript, with everything in it): ${SRC} (main session, JSON Lines; line N of the staged main file sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl is line N of this file) and ${SRC_DIR}/ (sub-agent sessions under subagents/workflows/<run>/, run records under workflows/<run>.json).
Private configuration of the export: ${CONFIG} (never to be published; it holds the private terms as regular expressions, the withheld line ranges, and the list of lines withheld by hand). The exporter is ${S}/ai-export/export_sessions.py.
Your scratch directory: ${S}/ai-review3/privacy
${COMMON}

The configured terms (private_keywords, private_tokens, literals, model names) have been searched in the whole staged directory: zero hits outside the request as typed. Do not repeat that search. Your job is what a term list cannot find. Find anything still readable in the staged directory that should not be published:
- content of the unrelated request or of the third-party documents it dealt with, in ANY wording: paraphrases, summaries, translated or abbreviated terms, fragments, names of people, companies, teams, projects, products or customers, amounts, dates and periods, document titles, file and folder names, job and task names, identifiers and URLs of documents, mail subjects;
- the candidate's e-mail address or identity beyond the GitHub account name; identifiers of the account; other repositories or organisations of the account; the reviewer's name, address or company;
- credentials, tokens, keys, cookies, signed URLs;
- names of AI models.

Where to look, in this order:
1. Main session, lines 6380 to the end: this part is new since the last review. Here the session read the results of two earlier reviews of this export (results that describe the withheld material), fixed the export, and wrote about it. Read the assistant's own prose, its notes, its commands, the tool outputs that are still shown, and the two compaction summaries (search for entries with "isCompactSummary"). Compare with the source to see what was withheld and judge whether what remains gives anything away.
2. The files of the two review runs: sessions/subagents/wf_ce880d66-b3c/ and sessions/subagents/wf_64f4f895-96e/ (run.json, journal.jsonl, script.js, every agent-*.jsonl.gz, *.meta.json). They are meant to show the task of each reviewer and a skeleton of its session, nothing of its working steps or results.
3. The generated files: sessions/readable/ (the parts that cover lines 5200 to the end), tool-actions.csv, session-index.csv, sessions/redaction-report.json, sessions/subagents/README.md.
4. The rest of the main session by a method of your own that is NOT a search for the configured terms. For example: collect the words (also 2- to 4-character Chinese sequences, capitalised names, numbers with units, file names) that are frequent in the withheld lines of the source and absent or rare in the assignment part, and look for them in the staged files; compare source and staged text of the entries just before and after each withheld range; look at short pieces of text that survive between two markers; look at the fields the tool stores beside the visible ones (toolUseResult, wireToolInputs, rendered, renderedInHumanTurn, attachment fields, compactMetadata, queue-operation content).
5. Over-redaction: places where a prompt typed by the candidate about the assignment, or assignment content, was withheld without need (report as minor).

For each finding give the staged file, the line, the field, what kind of material it is, and which rule would remove it.`

const outsider = `You are a stranger on the internet who found a directory in a public git repository and wants to learn from it what its owner did not mean to tell.

The directory: ${OUTSIDER}
Read ONLY this directory. Do not open anything else on this machine: nothing under /root/.claude, nothing else under the scratchpad, not the repository. (A copy was made for you so that nothing but the published files is in reach; staying inside it is the point of the exercise.)
Your scratch directory: ${S}/ai-review3/outsider-notes (create it; keep your notes there)
${COMMON}

Try, with every technique you can think of, to find out:
1. What the "unrelated private request" was about, beyond what the candidate's own typed request (main session line 554) says: what documents were handled, about whom, from where, what was done with them, what they contained.
2. Who the third parties are: names of people, companies, teams, projects, products, customers; amounts, dates, titles.
3. Who the candidate is, beyond the GitHub account name that owns the repository: e-mail address, real name, employer, location, other repositories or organisations, identifiers of accounts.
4. Who set the assignment: company, reviewer's name or address.
5. Any credential: tokens, keys, passwords that are not obviously test fixtures of the assignment, cookies, signed URLs.
6. Which AI models were used, by name (the export says it replaces them by letters).
7. Anything else personal or confidential.

Techniques to use (not a complete list): read around every kind of marker and see what the surrounding text gives away; list all capitalised names, non-English text, URLs, host names, e-mail-like strings, long hex or base64-looking strings (decode them), file and directory names, numbers with currency or units; look into every .gz file (zcat), the CSV files, the reading copy, the JSON reports, the scripts under export/; look at sizes and counts in the markers and in redaction-report.json and say what can be inferred from them; look at time stamps; look for the same thing said in a second place where it was not replaced (a summary, a notice, a command, an error message, a file path).

Report what you could establish, how, and where (file, line). Also report honestly what you could NOT find out although you tried - that is a result too. If a marker's reason text itself tells more than it should, say so.`

const facts = `You check the factual statements of the documents in a directory before it is published. Wrong facts in these documents will be held against the candidate.

Staged directory: ${STAGE}
- README.md, decision-log.md, completeness-declaration.md, session-index.csv, tool-actions.csv
- sessions/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9.jsonl (the exported main session), sessions/readable/ (reading copy, generated), sessions/subagents/ (README.md, one directory per run), sessions/tool-results/, sessions/redaction-report.json
- export/ (the two scripts and runs.json)
The tool's own transcript, if you need to compare: ${SRC} (same line numbers as the exported main session) and ${SRC_DIR}/.
The repository the directory will be added to (read only; use "git -C ${REPO} log" and "git -C ${REPO} show" to check commits): ${REPO}
The requirements of the assignment for this directory ("section 5"): ${S}/ai-export/section5.txt
Your scratch directory: ${S}/ai-review3/facts
${COMMON}

import hashlib, json, os, re, sys

MARK = re.compile(r'\[REDACTED: [^\]]*\]')
def files(root):

a, b = files(old), files(new)

    if 'readable/' in k or k.endswith('.gz'):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""

The tool keeps one JSON Lines file per session (one JSON object per line: prompts, assistant
messages, tool calls, tool results, harness notices) and one more per sub-agent it started. This
script copies those files line by line and changes a line only where one of the rules below
applies. Every change leaves a marker of the form "[REDACTED: reason]" in place of the removed
text, so the position, the kind and the size of what was removed stay visible.

What is replaced
  1. Binary payloads: base64 image data and the opaque signatures attached to reasoning blocks.
  2. Material of the tool vendor: the built-in system prompt, bundled reference texts, and the

  3. Private data that has nothing to do with the assignment: entries (given by line number in
     the private configuration) that belong to another request handled in the same session, and
     any later line that names it.
  4. Identifiers: the candidate's e-mail address, account identifiers, model identifiers.

Everything that names private terms lives in a configuration file that is not part of the
repository (the terms themselves are what must not be published). The rules are generic.

shows the same line numbers. Sub-agent sessions are named `<run>/agent-<id>` as in
[`session-index.csv`](session-index.csv). Commits are in this repository.

## Who decided what

The record shows a short list of inputs by the candidate and a long list of actions by the
assistant. This is everything the candidate typed:

| Line | Time (UTC) | What |
| --- | --- | --- |

decisions are marked **delegated** below. Where the candidate decided, the entry says so.

substantial work. The record shows the tool's notice of that mode, not how it was switched on.

most of its own output was corrected.

请你帮我做一下这个任务：# Project Spec: Multi-Tenant Certificate Admin Console

Build an internal admin console for a multi-tenant training platform where tenant admins review course completions, issue certificates, revoke them, and export certificate data.

## 1. Tech Stack & Constraints
- **Backend**: Go, Python, or Node.js with a mainstream framework. Use SQLite, MySQL, or PostgreSQL (persistent storage required, no in-memory-only DB).
- **Frontend**: Vue 3 or React (Vite optional).
- **Startup**: Provide one documented command that installs/uses declared dependencies, initializes demo data, and starts the full app. Optionally provide a second command to run verification tests.
- **Actor Context**: No login UI needed. Seed one admin per tenant and identify the actor via an HTTP header or token (e.g., `X-Actor-Email`).
- **Scope Control**: Do not add production auth, cloud deployment, notifications, or unrelated features. Prioritize core behavioral correctness over visual polish.

## 2. Seed / Demo Data Requirements
- Two tenants:
  - `East` with timezone `Australia/Sydney`
  - `West` with timezone `Australia/Perth`
- Two admins (each bound strictly to their own tenant):
  - `alice@east.test` -> `East`
  - `bob@west.test` -> `West`

===== evaluate:scenarios: verdicts {'met': 28, 'partly met': 4}; findings 9
SUMMARY: I started the clean clone with `npm start` (port 3000) and followed every step of the README section "Reproducing A1–A7 by hand". I ran the commands verbatim, with one change: I wrote the /tmp output files to my scratch directory instead. Every output matched what the README says. I then ran my own checks: Node and curl scripts, my own read-only SQLite queries, and Playwright in Chromium for the UI. The demo data and A1, A2, A3, A4, A6 and A7 met the Expected column, including concurrent bursts and a byte-for-byte comparison of the exports against an independent query. A5 passed: the API, UI and CSV show 2026-01-11 00:30 (East) and 2026-01-10 21:30 (West). Local-date ordering is correct on certificates I inserted around midnight myself, but an evaluator cannot reproduce that ordering on the running app; the README sends them to the candidate's own test instead. All defects I found are documentation gaps or nits, and none breaks a requirement. The one point that depends on interpretation is "without changing the default quick-start dataset": the seeded rows stay unchanged row for row, but the default command writes into the quick-start database, so the console then shows 100,007 East certificates and 10 extra courses until `--clear` or `db:reset` is run.
  [partly met] 4 demo data (5): A command or script that can generate 100,000 certificate rows for one tenant without changing the default quick-start dataset.
      evidence: `npm run generate:east` took 3.3-3.8 s and added exactly 100,000 East certificates. My dump script (work/dump.py) hashed every non-generated row of tenants, admins, courses, learners, enrollments, certificates, audit_events and bulk_issue_operations before generating, after generating and after `--clear`: all hashes were identical, including tenants.last_serial. `--clear` brings the counts back to 11 certificates and 13 audit events. `--db <file>` generates into a separate file (it created a seeded copy plus the 100k rows in work/load.sqlite). Reading 1 (the seeded rows are not modified): met. Reading 2 (the quick-start app is unchanged): not met by the default command. It writes into data/cert-admin.sqlite, so GET /api/certificates for Alice then reports total 100,007 instead of 7. The course picker and /api/courses gain 10 '(load test)' courses. The default list (issued desc) puts generated rows first. This lasts until `--clear` or `npm run db:reset`.
      readme: 4. Load-test data
  [partly met] A3 README: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A3).
      evidence: README steps gave '409 idempotency_key_reused', 'first result intact' and 'still 2 operations', as documented. They only show the 'different course' case, not a different payload for the same course (the scenario says 'different course or request payload'); I verified that case myself.
      readme: Reproducing A1–A7 by hand › A3
  [partly met] A5 README: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A5).
      evidence: The README conversion steps work: the seeded certs 1 and 8 have exactly 2026-01-10T13:30Z, as documented in section 2. The README itself says these lines do not show the ordering rule, and sends the evaluator to the candidate's own test (`node --test ... 'tenant-local calendar date'`, which passed in 0.5 s). There is no documented way to create certificates at chosen instants on the running app, so the ordering part cannot be reproduced through the API or UI.
      readme: Reproducing A1–A7 by hand › A5
  [partly met] A6 README: Your README must explain how to reproduce each scenario (A6).
      evidence: The README steps worked (generate 3.8 s; exports 0.51 s and 0.37 s; cmp identical; 25,481 lines; 'ties in ascending id order'; six list timings of 5-8 ms). However, the list-during-export step prints no export start/end times, so it does not show that the list requests overlapped the exports. Nothing checks the CSV row set against the data.
      readme: Reproducing A1–A7 by hand › A6

      repro: Fresh clone: `npm start`; in a second terminal `npm run generate:east`; `curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' 'http://localhost:3000/api/certificates?pageSize=1'` and `curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' http://localhost:3000/api/courses`
      expected: Under the stricter reading of 'without changing the default quick-start dataset', the quick-start app still shows its 7 East certificates and 3 courses.
      actual: total 100007. /api/courses lists 10 extra '(load test)' courses, and the default list (newest first) shows generated rows ahead of the demo rows. The seeded rows themselves are byte-identical (verified by hashing), and `--clear`, `db:reset` or `--db <other file>` restore the original view.
      suggestion: Make generating into a separate file the default (or the documented primary path), or state explicitly that 'quick-start dataset' means the seeded rows, not what the running console shows.
  FINDING 2 [minor] A5 ordering rule cannot be reproduced on the running app
      repro: README › Reproducing A5: the curl lines only show the conversion; the README says the ordering case is 'built and checked ... by one test of the suite' and gives `(cd backend && node --test ... --test-name-pattern='tenant-local calendar date' test/acceptance.test.js)`
      expected: An evaluator can see, through the API and UI, that list sorting and CSV use the tenant-local date (e.g. seeded certificates on the same UTC day but different local days, or a documented way to create them).
      actual: No seeded pair shows the difference, and there is no documented way to create certificates at a chosen instant. Reproducing it means trusting the candidate's own test. I had to insert rows directly into SQLite to check it (it does sort correctly).
      suggestion: Seed one pair per tenant around local midnight (lower id issued later in UTC), or document a script that inserts them.
  FINDING 3 [minor] README reproduction steps write to and delete shared /tmp paths
      repro: README › Reproducing A2/A3/A6: `rm -f /tmp/a2-*.json`, `-o /tmp/a2-{}.json`, `-o /tmp/e1.csv`, and at the end `rm -f /tmp/a2-*.json /tmp/e1.csv /tmp/e2.csv`
      expected: Steps that stay inside the project or a private temp directory (e.g. `mktemp -d`).
      actual: Fixed names in /tmp. On a shared machine (two evaluators at once, as here) runs overwrite or delete each other's files, and the A3 `cmp` can compare against another person's answer. I had to change the paths to run the steps safely.
      suggestion: Use `T=$(mktemp -d)` and `$T/...` throughout.
  FINDING 4 [nit] A6 README step does not show that the list request overlapped the export
      repro: README › A6: `for i in 1 2 3; do curl ... export.csv -o /dev/null & done; for i in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do curl -w '%{time_total}s ' ... ; done; echo; wait`
      expected: Output that shows each list request was sent and answered while an export was still streaming.
      actual: Only list durations are printed (5-8 ms). Export start/end times are not shown, so overlap is assumed, not demonstrated. My own timed check confirmed the overlap (list answered at 78 ms, export ended at 435 ms).
      suggestion: Print timestamps (e.g. `date +%s.%N`) at the start and end of the export and of each list request.
  FINDING 5 [nit] A3 README step covers only 'different course', not 'different payload'
      repro: README › Reproducing A3 only sends `{"courseId": 3}` with key demo-par
      expected: The scenario says 'a different course or request payload'; the reproduction should show both.
      actual: The same-course payload change is not shown. I verified it myself: `{"courseId":1,"note":"x"}` with the used key -> 409, nothing written.
      suggestion: Add one line with the same courseId and an extra or changed field.
  FINDING 6 [nit] README A6 does not check the CSV row set against the data
      repro: README › A6 compares e1.csv with e2.csv and counts lines only
      expected: A step that shows the CSV contains exactly the matching rows (e.g. compare the line count with the list `total` for the same query).
      actual: Only the two exports are compared and the line count is printed against a hard-coded 25,481. My own DB comparison found the set and the order correct.
      suggestion: Add `curl ... /api/certificates?$Q&pageSize=1 | grep -o '"total":[0-9]*'` next to `wc -l`.
  FINDING 7 [nit] CSV and list show identical local times for two different instants at the DST fold, with no offset
      repro: `curl -s -H 'X-Actor-Email: alice@east.test' 'http://localhost:3000/api/certificates/export.csv?sort=issued&order=asc'`
      expected: Distinguishable times (or an offset column) for EAST-0000003 (2026-04-04T15:30Z) and EAST-0000004 (2026-04-04T16:30Z).
      actual: Both rows print '2026-04-05 02:30' in the CSV and in the list. Only the detail drawer adds 'UTC+11:00' / 'UTC+10:00'. This is correct local wall-clock time but ambiguous; the requirement does not ask for more.
      suggestion: Optionally add the UTC offset or an ISO UTC column to the CSV.
  FINDING 8 [nit] Unknown query parameters are silently ignored despite README wording
      repro: `curl -s -w ' %{http_code}' -H 'X-Actor-Email: bob@west.test' 'http://localhost:3000/api/certificates?foo=bar&pageSize=1'` and `...?tenant=East`
      expected: README section 5: 'Query parameters are validated: an unknown value is a 400, never silently ignored'. A reader may expect unknown parameter names to be refused as well.
      actual: 200; `foo` and `tenant` are ignored (harmless for isolation, because the tenant is never read from the query). Only unknown values of known parameters (e.g. sort=bogus) are 400.
      suggestion: Say 'unknown value of a known parameter', or reject unknown parameter names.
  FINDING 9 [nit] --clear leaves the database file at full size
      repro: `npm run generate:east` then `npm run generate:east -- --clear`; `ls -la data/`
      expected: Not required, but the README says `--clear` 'leaves exactly the rows that were there without it'.
      actual: The rows are restored, but cert-admin.sqlite stays at about 88 MB (plus a 16 MB WAL) until `npm run db:reset`.
      suggestion: Mention it, or VACUUM after --clear.
  NOT CHECKED: ["`npm test` and the repository's own tests (deliberately not used as evidence; only the single A5 test the README points to was run, to follow the README)", 'Behaviour with two server processes on one database (README claims cross-process safety for A2/A7)', "UI 'Retry safely' flow after a lost answer, and reload persistence of the bulk-issue attempt", 'Export timing under heavier concurrent load (more than 3 simultaneous full exports); all measured exports were under 0.6 s on this shared machine, so no repeat was needed', 'Node 20 / the node:sqlite fallback driver (only better-sqlite3 on Node 22.23.5 was used)', '`npm run dev` and the PORT/HOST settings', 'A6 with a seed other than the default (`--seed N`) or a count other than 100,000']
===== evaluate:scope: verdicts {'met': 25, 'could not verify': 1}; findings 4
SUMMARY: I ran exactly `PORT=3111 npm start` in the clean clone. It installed the dependencies, built the React UI, created the SQLite demo database and served both UI and API in about 5 s (with a warm npm cache). I then tested every workflow of section 3 in real Chromium with Playwright: actor switching, search by name and serial, paging, sorting every column both ways, and loading, empty and error states (delayed or failed requests, stopped server). I also tested bulk issue: double-click, repeated Enter, forced re-click, a lost answer followed by a safe retry, and a failed outcome caused by a fault I injected into the database. On the detail drawer I checked the fields, cancel, Escape and confirmed revocation, and the audit events in the drawer, the API and the database. For CSV export I exported three search and sort combinations from the UI and compared each file with the list on screen. A stop and restart showed the data persists. `npm test` passed once (193 API and 257 UI tests, exit 0, 79 s). Every requirement sentence of sections 2 and 3 that was in my scope is met. The 100,000-row part of the export row is left to the other evaluator. I found only nits: the Loading badge covers the Status column header, failed outcomes give a generic reason, the CSV date includes a time, and two rows show the same local time at the DST change with nothing to tell them apart.
  [could not verify] 3 CSV export (c): Handle 100,000-row exports as specified in A6.
      evidence: Assigned to the other evaluator. I only confirmed that the UI export works on the demo data (above).
      readme: Section 4, Section 6
  FINDING 1 [nit] List 'Loading…' badge covers the STATUS column header
      repro: PORT=3111 npm start; in Chromium, delay GET /api/certificates?* by 3 s (route interception), then type 'a' in Search on the Certificates page.
      expected: The loading indicator does not hide table content.
      actual: The 'Loading…' pill sits over the STATUS header, which reads 'ST'. Screenshot: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/61a877e9-483e-575a-b7cf-c5b8e94decb9/scratchpad/req-check/scope/work/08-loading.png
      suggestion: Place the indicator outside the header row, or reserve space for it.
  FINDING 2 [nit] Failed per-learner outcome gives only a generic reason
      repro: While the server runs, add a SQLite trigger on data/cert-admin.sqlite: CREATE TRIGGER eval_fail BEFORE INSERT ON certificates WHEN NEW.learner_id=10 BEGIN SELECT RAISE(ABORT,'x'); END; then, as bob, bulk issue West Safety 101 in the UI.
      expected: Reading 1: 'failed' needs a reason, like 'skipped'. Reading 2: the requirement only names the outcomes issued, skipped and failed.
      actual: Emily Davis shows outcome Failed, reason code issue_failed, and a generic message ('unexpected error ... the server log has the details'). The actual cause is only in the server log. This satisfies reading 2, and reading 1 only with a generic reason. Screenshot work/15-bulk-failed-outcome.png
      suggestion: Acceptable as is; could expose a safe classification of the cause.
  FINDING 3 [nit] CSV 'tenant-local issue date' column contains date and time
      repro: In the UI, click Export CSV and open the file.
      expected: 'Tenant-local issue date' (and A5's 'CSV use the tenant-local calendar date') can be read as date only (YYYY-MM-DD) or as a local date-time.
      actual: The column is 'Issue Date (Australia/Sydney)' with values like '2026-01-11 00:30'. The tenant-local calendar date is correct, but the time is included. This satisfies the date-time reading, not a strict date-only reading.
      suggestion: Document the choice, or add a separate date-only column.
  FINDING 4 [nit] Two different instants show the same local time in the list at the DST end, with no way to tell them apart
      repro: As alice, view the Certificates list sorted by Issue date.
      expected: Rows with distinct instants are distinguishable in the list (for example by offset), or are knowingly shown as equal.
      actual: EAST-0000003 (2026-04-04T15:30Z) and EAST-0000004 (16:30Z) both show '2026-04-05 02:30'. Only the detail drawer shows UTC+11:00 versus UTC+10:00. The sort order is correct (by instant).
      suggestion: Show the offset in the list for ambiguous local times.
  NOT CHECKED: ['The 100,000-row export (A6), which is assigned to the other evaluator', 'Startup time with a cold npm cache: the 5 s I measured used a warm cache on this machine', 'A true OS-level held Enter key with auto-repeat (I simulated 10 Enter presses plus a keydown/keyup)', 'Browsers other than Chromium, and screen readers', 'npm run dev, npm run db:reset and generate:east']

content.content:
## 4. Load-test data (100,000 certificates)

```bash
npm run generate:east                      # takes ~3 s; can run while the server is up
npm run generate:east -- --count 250000    # other volumes
npm run generate:east -- --clear           # remove the generated rows
npm run generate:east -- --db /tmp/load.sqlite   # work on a separate database file instead
                                                 # (start the app on it with DB_PATH=/tmp/load.sqlite npm start)
npm run db:reset -- --db /tmp/load.sqlite        # and back to the quick-start dataset in that file
```

The generator **does not modify the quick-start dataset**. The generated certificates belong to
their own 10 generated courses and 10,000 generated learners (flagged `is_generated = 1`) and are
numbered in a serial range of their own (`EAST-LT-0000001` …). The seeded tenants (their serial
counters included), admins, courses, learners, enrollments, certificates and audit events are left
exactly as they were - asserted row by row in the test suite - so `Safety 101`, `Alex Lee` and
every demo scenario behave as before, and the next certificate issued through the app is
`EAST-0000008` with or without the load-test data. Re-running the generator replaces the previous
generated set, so the count never piles up; `--clear` removes it and leaves exactly the rows that
were there without it; `npm run db:reset` restores the pristine dataset and shrinks the database
file back to the size of a newly created one.

The generator writes everything in one transaction. While it runs, a server on the same database
keeps answering reads (which see the old rows until the generator commits) and retries of finished
bulk issues; new writes wait for it and complete as soon as it is done.

The data is built to contain many equal sort keys: ~2,500 distinct learner names for 100,000
certificates, 10 course titles, ~150 certificates per calendar day, and batches of 25 certificates
that share the exact same issue instant (like a real bulk issue). It is generated from a seeded
PRNG, so every run produces the same rows, serial numbers included (`--seed N` gives another set).

The generator writes everything in one transaction. While it runs, a server on the same database
keeps answering reads (which see the old rows until the generator commits) and retries of finished
bulk issues; new writes wait for it and complete as soon as it is done.

The data is built to contain many equal sort keys: ~2,500 distinct learner names for 100,000
certificates, 10 course titles, ~150 certificates per calendar day, and batches of 25 certificates
that share the exact same issue instant (like a real bulk issue). It is generated from a seeded
PRNG, so every run produces the same rows, serial numbers included (`--seed N` gives another set).

## 10. Known defects and unfinished work

**Known defects** - behaviour that is wrong or surprising, and known:

- *A very large bulk issue holds every other request up while it runs.* It is one synchronous
  transaction. Measured: issuing to 20,000 eligible learners takes about one second, and a list
  request sent meanwhile waits that long. At the sizes of the specification (a course roster) this
  is milliseconds.
- *List requests are linear in the tenant's size where the export is not.* The substring search of
  a list request, and its deep pages (`page=4000`), scan the tenant's rows in one piece: tens of
  milliseconds at 100,000 certificates, during which other requests wait.
- *A double click on text in a list row opens the certificate instead of selecting the word.* A
  click on a row opens the drawer at once; selecting by dragging works, and the same text can be
  selected in the drawer.
- *Leaving with the browser's Back button while a revocation is on its way* closes the
  confirmation without its outcome message. The request is not cancelled; the list shows the result.
- *A download cut short is not noticed by every client.* The server resets the connection of a
  download it gives up, but netcat and raw Node.js sockets report a reset after data as a normal
  end; and a client that half-closes its connection (`nc -N`) or reads more slowly than a few kB/s
  for five minutes is treated as gone (see *Export without blocking* in section 7).
- *Idempotency keys are kept for ever.* Nothing expires them, so the table grows by one row per
  bulk issue.
- *A SIGTERM to the `npm` process does not stop the app.* `npm start` and `npm run dev` are meant
  to be stopped with Ctrl+C, which reaches every process they started. `kill <pid of npm>` ends
  npm alone: the shell npm runs its scripts in does not pass the signal on, and the server keeps
  running. Signal the process group, or the `node` process itself.
- *In `npm run dev` the API does not come back by itself after a syntax error has been fixed.*
  Node's watch mode stops watching a file that failed to load: save any other file of the backend,
  or restart the command.

**Not verified** - there is no evidence either way:

- Browsers other than Chromium, and real screen readers. Keyboard operation, focus handling and the
  accessibility tree were checked in Chromium only.
- Windows. The commands and tests were run on Linux (Node 20.20, 22.23 and 24.22).
- More than 100,000 certificates per tenant (the generator accepts up to 2,000,000).
